units.function: HTTP compatibility tests ensuring the legacy member route still prevents Owner self-lockout and preserves custom permission grants after the granular-permissions upgrade.
units.dependencyDirection: Express access routes receive an authenticated board actor, validate a member patch, call AccessService, then persist CompanyMembership and PrincipalPermissionGrant state plus activity records.
units.keyDataModels: Board user actor, Company membership role/status, principal permission key with optional Project scope and granting user, and member PATCH response/error.
units.lifecycle: An Owner cannot demote themself through the role-only route; changing another member from admin to operator updates the role but retains an existing scoped task-assignment grant and its grantor provenance.
units.testAssessment: Two integration cases cover self-lockout and custom-grant preservation. Missing are actual authentication middleware, cross-Company IDs, non-owner actors, last-owner versus self distinction, status/archive changes, concurrent owner demotions, grant escalation after role downgrade, activity-log content, CSRF and transaction rollback. The fixture injects an Owner who is also instance admin, so route authorization separation is weakly exercised.
units.designRationale: Preserve safety and backward compatibility while moving from coarse roles to additive scoped grants, without silently erasing administrator-authored exceptions on a role-only update.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs stable human access administration through schema upgrades while preventing ownership lockout and retaining explicit, attributable exceptions.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the self/last-owner invariant and separation between role-only and role-plus-grant commands. Add optimistic versioning, authenticated actor/Company checks, immutable AccessDecision receipts and a post-change effective-permission diff. Role downgrade should flag grants that exceed the new role baseline for explicit confirmation rather than silently retain or erase them.
units.responsibilityConflict: The route preserves who granted the custom scope but does not require an accountable approver for the role/grant combination, nor prove that running Agent capabilities and sessions reflect the change. A demoted member may retain meaningful powers without a surfaced responsibility review.
evidence: 38c185fb8b50f909d29c0b62783731a3b326d021 Add agent permissions and controls plan (#6386)

units.function: Embedded-Postgres tests for Company human membership lifecycle, last-Owner invariants, role-default/scoped permission grants, member archival and Work reassignment, instance access protection, compatibility backfill and membership copying during Company import.
units.dependencyDirection: AccessService mutates CompanyMembership, PrincipalPermissionGrant, InstanceUserRole and Issue assignment state; role-default helpers define baseline grants; a compatibility backfill derives memberships/grants from legacy human and Agent rows.
units.keyDataModels: Human/Agent principal membership and role/status, instance admin, permission key plus opaque scope/grantor, open versus terminal Issue assignee, Agent lifecycle status and compatibility/import counters.
units.lifecycle: The last active Owner cannot be demoted or suspended; archiving a member clears grants, reassigns open Work to a chosen human and returns it to todo while completed history keeps the original assignee; self, Owner/admin and instance-admin Company access receive removal protection; role defaults grant environment management only to Owner/admin; idempotent backfill adds missing human grants without replacing a custom scope and adds active memberships only for non-terminal Agents; import copies active humans with target role defaults.
units.testAssessment: Nine substantial integration cases cover last-owner safety, archival/history, protected access, role defaults, idempotent migration, Agent status filtering, import and scoped-grant preservation. Missing are multi-Owner concurrency and database locking, authorization of every service caller, SSO/HR deprovisioning, session/token/active-Run revocation, reassignment acceptance and responsibility contract, pending approvals, tasks with multiple roles, deny/expiry/conditions, separation of duties, grant versioning, immutable audit, import consent, duplicate identities and rollback across membership/grant/Issue updates. Agent membership is backfilled but effective Agent grants are not asserted.
units.designRationale: Preserve at least one administrator, soft-delete people to retain history, keep open work owned after offboarding, evolve roles into grants idempotently and avoid replacing explicit scoped policy during upgrades.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS requires first-class human employment/membership and accountable ownership lifecycle alongside Agents, with offboarding that preserves history but immediately removes authority and reassigns unfinished responsibility.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the last-owner invariant, archival-not-deletion, open-versus-historical Work treatment, grantor provenance, scoped-grant preservation and idempotent compatibility migration. Extend to IdentityPort/HR or enterprise directory binding, employment status, responsibility-contract transfer/acceptance, session/runtime/secret revocation, time-bound/conditional grants, separation-of-duties policy and immutable before/after audit. Company import must require explicit target-owner confirmation and map identities rather than automatically reproducing authority.
units.responsibilityConflict: Reassignment changes assignee and todo state but records no acceptance by the new accountable human or transfer evidence. Offboarding clears database grants without proving active tokens, Agent runs or external systems were revoked. Import can grant active target access from source membership without tested consent, and role defaults do not express legal/business accountability.

units.function: Minimal shared-schema tests for user profile image URLs and defaulting omitted combined member grants.
units.dependencyDirection: Server tests directly exercise shared Zod validators used by profile and combined membership/permission request routes.
units.keyDataModels: User display name/image URL and combined membershipRole/grants update payload.
units.lifecycle: HTTP(S) and Paperclip asset paths are accepted as profile images, data URIs are rejected, and omitted grants in a combined member update become an empty list.
units.testAssessment: Three narrow cases cover happy-path URLs, one dangerous URI family and default grants. Missing are javascript/file/ftp/protocol-relative URLs, exact asset path grammar, URL length/control characters, image-fetch SSRF behavior, Unicode names and the critical semantic distinction between an absent grants field and an explicitly empty list. Defaulting absence to [] can turn a partial update into grant deletion.
units.designRationale: Avoid large inline avatar payloads and normalize combined access-update inputs for simpler service code.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs safe profile resources and unambiguous patch semantics for high-impact access changes.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE ONLY. Use a managed AssetRef or tightly allowlisted HTTPS policy rather than arbitrary display URLs when servers fetch content. Preserve tri-state patch semantics: omitted grants means unchanged, explicit [] means revoke all, and replacement requires version/confirmation. Do not copy this combined-update default.
units.responsibilityConflict: A validator default can erase grants without the caller explicitly requesting revocation, obscuring intent and responsibility. Profile validation is unrelated to identity proof and does not bind an image asset to an authenticated person.

units.function: Tests Paperclip's responsible-user stamping for activity rows, including direct human actions and a fallback chain across heartbeat run, Issue, Agent API key, Company default and Issue creator.
units.dependencyDirection: The activity publication helper accepts actor/run/Issue/API-key context, reads operational tables through the database port, derives one responsibleUserId, persists it on ActivityLog and queues a post-commit publication.
units.keyDataModels: Activity actorType/actorId/action/entity, heartbeat run responsible user, Issue responsible user and creator, Agent API key responsible user, Company default responsible user and post-commit activity publication.
units.lifecycle: Human actions are attributed directly; Agent/system actions prefer explicit run attribution, then Issue attribution, then active API-key attribution, Company default and finally Issue creator. Malformed UUID-backed references are ignored, and the selected value is stamped when the activity row is written.
units.testAssessment: Nine focused cases exercise every fallback, malformed identifiers and one embedded-Postgres persistence path. Missing are tenant predicates on every lookup, inactive/revoked API keys, changed responsibility after run creation, null/unresolved attribution, transaction/publication failure, spoofed actor input, simultaneous contract changes, immutable history and distinction between initiator, observed actor, operator, approver and accountable human.
units.designRationale: Make Agent-originated activity explainable to a human operator even when the immediate actor is non-human, while preserving a compact column that audit views can filter.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must connect every executable action to its initiating principal and accountable human without losing the exact work, permission, data, approval, evidence and result context.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the ordered lookup as a best-effort operational attribution signal only. Store explicit, versioned ResponsibilityContract and WorkExecution references at authorization time; separately record observed actor, credential principal, initiating human, accountable human and approver. Unresolved attribution must remain explicit rather than silently becoming a Company default.
units.responsibilityConflict: A single inferred responsibleUserId conflates technical attribution with accepted organizational responsibility. Company default and Issue creator fallbacks can assign liability to someone who neither accepted the work nor approved the action, and later mutable table state is not proof of the contract effective when execution occurred.

b07b2994 stamp responsible users on activity logs

units.function: Route-level tests for Company activity, all-actor audit access tiers, Issue-run lookup, activity creation authorization and cross-tenant heartbeat-run existence-oracle resistance.
units.dependencyDirection: Express routes consume authenticated actor context and AccessService decisions, then call ActivityService, AgentActionAuditService, IssueService and HeartbeatService; the basic audit response is field-redacted before returning to the client.
units.keyDataModels: Company-scoped actor, access decision, audit actor scope/filter, activity attribution fields, Issue identifier, heartbeat run, list limit and basic/full response access tier.
units.lifecycle: A basic Company reader can inspect redacted all-actor events but cannot use attribution filters; an explicitly permitted reader receives full attribution. Company lists default to 100 and cap at 500. Issue identifiers are normalized before run lookup. Activity creation checks Company access. Cross-tenant and nonexistent run lookups both return 200 with an empty list, after anonymous callers are rejected, to avoid an existence oracle.
units.testAssessment: Nine route tests cover tiered disclosure, filter gating, limits, identifier resolution, write authorization and indistinguishable cross-tenant/not-found responses. Missing are cursor behavior for the ordinary activity endpoint, stable structured error codes, malformed/oversized filters, field-level policy evolution, response schema contracts, actor spoofing on create, rate limiting, CSRF, audit of denied queries, full middleware integration and leakage through timing or related entity fields.
units.designRationale: Offer a useful operational feed to broad Company readers while restricting sensitive Agent/run/human attribution, and prevent tenant membership probing through resource existence responses.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs separately governed operational status and responsibility evidence views, safe tenant boundaries and stable APIs consumable by its independent Web and Connector ecosystem.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the two-tier projection, filter authorization and indistinguishable existence response. Define policy-versioned field projections, cursor pagination, structured error codes and immutable access receipts. Separate a broad operational activity stream from the narrowly authorized ResponsibilityLedger rather than redacting one row shape ad hoc.
units.responsibilityConflict: The basic feed intentionally removes responsibleUserId, runId and details, so it cannot answer the product's responsibility-chain question. Conversely the full feed exposes raw details as a unit instead of applying data classification and purpose-bound field policy. The create surface is only shown checking Company access, not authority to assert the supplied actor/action/evidence semantics.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres tests for ordered activity listing, compact Issue-run ledger projections and asynchronous liveness backfill from run-bound comments and document revisions.
units.dependencyDirection: ActivityService reads ActivityLog, HeartbeatRun, Issue, comment and document/revision relations; it normalizes provider-shaped usage/results for API projection and can persist derived liveness fields back onto completed heartbeat runs.
units.keyDataModels: ActivityLog timestamp/action, heartbeat run context/usage/result/liveness/continuation, Issue status, run-bound Issue comment, document revision createdByRunId and continuation-summary document key.
units.lifecycle: Company activity is returned newest first with a limit. Issue-run views omit context snapshots and normalize a small allowlist of token, cost, billing and timeout fields. Completed runs missing liveness are classified and persisted; same-run concrete comments or document revisions can establish progress, while other-run revisions and continuation summaries are excluded and plan-only text stays non-evidence.
units.testAssessment: Five database integration cases validate ordering, payload compaction, persistence of a completed classification and two important false-positive exclusions. Missing are cursor pagination, deterministic ordering on timestamp ties, currency/provider provenance, invalid/negative/overflow usage, redaction of secrets in allowed fields, concurrent backfill, failure retry, immutable source hashes, deleted/edited comments, artifact/evidence authorization, all liveness classes and proof that classification changes cannot rewrite historical accountability.
units.designRationale: Keep the Issue run ledger fast and bounded despite arbitrary provider payloads, and repair older or incomplete runs using concrete artifacts instead of trusting an Agent's prose summary as proof of progress.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs efficient run projections and a defensible separation between self-reported status, observable work activity, evidence artifacts and final responsibility records.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the allowlisted payload projection, exact run binding and exclusion of continuation summaries. Keep liveness as a recomputable operational projection with classifier version and source references. Evidence admission must instead create immutable, content-addressed Evidence records with origin, authorization, retention and verification state; cost needs currency, provider and pricing provenance.
units.responsibilityConflict: Backfilled liveness mutates the run record and labels comments/revisions as concrete action evidence without an immutable admission receipt or accountable reviewer. It is a useful health inference, not proof that the authorized goal was satisfied, the data use was permitted or the result was approved. Compact cost fields also lose enough provenance to be unsuitable for contractual accounting.

units.function: Route tests for explicit Adapter model-cache refresh and environment-aware suppression of local OpenCode discovery on remote execution environments.
units.dependencyDirection: The authenticated Agent route resolves Company access and Environment metadata, looks up a server Adapter, then invokes its listModels or refreshModels capability; OpenCode discovery is conditionally replaced by package fallback metadata.
units.keyDataModels: Company-scoped Adapter type, refresh query flag, Environment driver/id, Adapter Model descriptor and optional refreshModels capability.
units.lifecycle: A refresh=1 request bypasses normal cached listing. Remote SSH environments receive static OpenCode fallback models without executing local discovery, while local environments invoke dynamic discovery.
units.testAssessment: Three route cases cover refresh dispatch and local-versus-remote OpenCode behavior. Missing are explicit permission assertions for refresh, cross-Company environment IDs, nonexistent environments, refresh storms/rate limits, timeout/cancellation, cache scope by Company/credential/environment, stale/error metadata, structured error codes and disclosure of models unavailable to the selected execution/data policy.
units.designRationale: Avoid probing the control-plane host for a runtime that actually lives remotely, while still allowing operators to refresh dynamic provider catalogs on demand.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must present model choices that are valid for the exact execution node, tenant credential and policy boundary without leaking or exercising credentials from the control plane.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the explicit refresh capability and environment-sensitive discovery. Route discovery through ModelProviderPort at the execution/data node; key cache entries by tenant, connector instance, credential reference, environment and policy version; return freshness/source/error codes and authorize/rate-limit refresh separately from read.
units.responsibilityConflict: The model list is treated as runtime availability, not as permission to use a model with specified data. The tests do not bind discovery or refresh to an accountable human, data authorization contract or immutable audit receipt.

units.function: Tests model catalogs across built-in Claude, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode Adapters, including live provider/CLI discovery, static fallbacks, caching, forced refresh and operator-declared model overrides.
units.dependencyDirection: The central Adapter facade delegates to Adapter-specific model discoverers, which read process environment credentials or execute a local CLI, merge dynamic results with package fallbacks and keep process-local caches; PAPERCLIP_ADAPTER_MODELS can override discovery per Adapter type.
units.keyDataModels: Adapter type, model id/label, provider API response, CLI discovery output, static fallback catalog, raw environment override and process-local cache.
units.lifecycle: Unknown and retired Adapters expose no models. Without credentials or after discovery failure, static catalogs remain available. Successful live/CLI discovery is cached and merged with fallback options; explicit refresh replaces cached discovery. A JSON environment map takes precedence, observes raw-value changes and fails soft when malformed.
units.testAssessment: Sixteen focused cases cover unknown/tombstoned types, credential-free behavior, provider success/failure, caching/refresh, CLI parsing and declared overrides. Missing are tenant/credential/environment cache isolation, secret-provider indirection, pagination, provider rate limits and retry, model retirement/capability metadata, regional/data-residency restrictions, malicious CLI output, command timeout, concurrent refresh, cache TTL, stable provenance and validation that declared models are actually usable.
units.designRationale: Keep setup resilient and useful offline while opportunistically showing newly available models, and give self-hosted operators a simple escape hatch when automatic discovery is incomplete.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs vendor-neutral model catalogs and switching without confusing technical availability with enterprise authorization, cost, residency or data-export eligibility.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the provider-specific discovery behind ModelProviderPort, static fallback merge and fail-soft semantics. Replace process-global environment credentials and caches with tenant-scoped SecretRef resolution and connector-node discovery; normalize capabilities, region, pricing provenance, lifecycle state and policy eligibility separately from display metadata. Operator declarations need schema validation and health verification.
units.responsibilityConflict: A listed model can be selected despite absent proof of data-use authorization, budget approval or responsible owner. Process environment keys and global caches risk cross-tenant coupling, and a silent static fallback can present stale or unauthorized choices without surfacing provenance to the approving human.

units.function: Tests the process-local server Adapter registry: external registration/removal, built-in override and pause fallback, model/capability exposure, runtime install commands, Hermes built-ins and session-management resolution.
units.dependencyDirection: Built-in Adapter packages and externally loaded ServerAdapterModule objects converge in one mutable registry; facade lookups select an active external override or built-in fallback and expose execution, environment test, configuration, model, skill, JWT and session capabilities.
units.keyDataModels: Adapter type/module, active external override, paused-override state, capability flags, ModelProfile, runtime command/install specification, model detection result and SessionManagement policy.
units.lifecycle: External modules register and unregister at runtime and may replace a built-in with the same type. Pausing an override restores built-in behavior. Capability flags and model profiles flow through lookup helpers. Built-ins can supply sandbox-aware npm installation commands. External modules keep an explicit session policy or, when omitted, inherit hardcoded policy for a matching built-in type.
units.testAssessment: Thirteen unit cases cover registry CRUD, overrides, pause fallback, several capability shapes, model profiles, install command construction and session-policy precedence. Missing are signature/provenance/version checks, duplicate registration races, persistence/restart behavior, compatibility negotiation, trust tiers, permission and egress manifests, crash isolation, unload with active runs, rollback, audit events, pinned package integrity and tests proving omission of a capability fails closed.
units.designRationale: Provide one extension surface for built-in and plugin Agent runtimes while retaining an emergency path back to known built-ins and compatibility defaults for older modules.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs equal multi-vendor Connectors with explicit capabilities, version negotiation, health, pause/resume/cancel/evidence behavior and safe lifecycle management across cloud and customer-local execution nodes.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the unified lookup, explicit capability declaration, pause fallback and module-owned session policy. Use a versioned ConnectorManifest plus installed ConnectorInstance records, signed provenance, trust tier, permissions/data-egress declaration and compatibility negotiation. Do not allow an external module to impersonate a built-in type; overrides must be explicit bindings with rollback and active-run drain semantics. Omitted safety capabilities fail closed.
units.responsibilityConflict: Type-name override and inherited session semantics can silently change execution behavior without a responsibility-contract revision or human approval. Capability flags describe mechanics but not authorized scopes, data contracts, evidence guarantees or accountable owner. Runtime install strings also lack demonstrated package pin/integrity evidence.

units.function: Route tests for Adapter catalog/capability and configuration-schema projection, legacy tombstones, organization access, hot installation, built-in override pause/removal and session-policy preservation.
units.dependencyDirection: Express routes project the active process registry and Adapter-provided schemas to clients; mutation routes call the plugin store and package loader, register the resulting server module and manage override state against built-ins.
units.keyDataModels: Adapter catalog entry/source/capabilities/ACP prerequisites, versioned ConfigSchema fields, external plugin installation record, active override, retired Adapter tombstone and SessionManagement policy.
units.lifecycle: Clients list normalized capabilities and fetch the active Adapter's schema. Retired types remain as model-less/schema-empty tombstones for stored-row compatibility. An instance admin can hot-install a package or local path, including an implementation with a built-in type; pause restores the built-in and deletion removes the external record while preserving the built-in.
units.testAssessment: Thirteen route tests cover capability projections, several built-in schemas, active override behavior, tombstones, one organization-access denial, hot-install parity and override removal. Missing are signed packages, exact version/integrity/SBOM, local-path traversal and symlink cases, install sandboxing, malicious schema/parser payloads, secret-field redaction, two-person approval, audit/rollback, active-run drain, concurrent mutation, stable error codes and compatibility negotiation.
units.designRationale: Expose enough headless metadata for a generic UI to configure diverse runtimes, preserve old database rows after Adapter retirement and allow operators to extend or recover runtime integrations without restarting the service.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a vendor-neutral Connector catalog and configuration contract that supports independent Web clients and upgrades without allowing third-party execution code to silently alter enterprise control-plane behavior.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the normalized capability/schema projection, explicit tombstones and pause-to-known-good rollback. Separate ConnectorPackage, signed ConnectorVersion and tenant ConnectorInstance; installation must verify provenance, license, digest, SBOM, compatibility and trust policy in an isolated plugin host. Bind an instance to a package explicitly rather than permitting type-name replacement, and never expose secret values through config schemas.
units.responsibilityConflict: An instance admin can introduce or replace executable code globally without demonstrated separation of duties or a responsibility-contract change. Capability booleans say what code can do, not what a tenant authorizes it to do; schema fields can describe credentials but do not establish custody, purpose or data-export approval.

units.function: Authorization tests for all Adapter code-management routes and a cloud-managed platform floor that prevents package install/reinstall even for instance administrators.
units.dependencyDirection: Route authorization consumes the instance-level actor before plugin store, child-process installer or package loader calls; deployment mode is inferred from a cloud tenant server-token environment setting and imposes an additional deny policy.
units.keyDataModels: Board actor, Company membership role, instance-admin flag, external Adapter installation record, six mutating operations and structured platform-managed denial detail code.
units.lifecycle: Company viewer/operator/admin members cannot install, disable, pause overrides, delete, reload or reinstall Adapter code. Instance admins can reach all six operations in ordinary self-hosted mode. In cloud-managed mode, install and reinstall remain forbidden and no installer/loader process is invoked.
units.testAssessment: Parameterized tests efficiently cover the full mutation surface, ordinary Company roles, positive instance-admin access and the managed-cloud install floor with side-effect assertions. Missing are anonymous/Agent/API-key actors, stale admin sessions, CSRF, step-up authentication, dual control, permission-specific roles, immutable decision audit, deployment-profile configuration validation, disable/reload platform floors, confused-deputy calls and TOCTOU between authorization and install.
units.designRationale: Treat runtime code installation as host administration rather than tenant administration, and reserve cloud package supply-chain control to the platform operator regardless of tenant-level authority.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must keep tenant governance separate from host code authority and enforce non-bypassable deployment-profile security floors across managed-cloud and self-hosted/local enterprise profiles.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the host-versus-tenant authority split, deny-before-side-effect discipline and deployment-profile floor. Represent profile policy as signed configuration rather than presence of a token environment variable; require step-up authentication, separation of duties for production installation, signed decision receipts, maintenance windows, rollback and active-run drain. Local enterprise can delegate package trust only through explicit policy.
units.responsibilityConflict: A single instance-admin boolean is too coarse for introducing executable supply-chain code and does not identify requester, approver and accountable operator separately. The cloud floor is strong, but ordinary self-hosted installation has no tested human approval/evidence chain.
evidence: c274f10abc0e3c60a47e6ac3f786443b0e197543 feat(server): computed owner instance-admin elevation for cloud-managed instances, behind platform floors (#10343)

units.function: Cross-Adapter compatibility tests for normalizing vendor session payloads, preserving ACP resume metadata and detecting textual unknown/unrecoverable-session failures that should trigger fresh-session recovery.
units.dependencyDirection: Each vendor Adapter owns a SessionCodec that translates persisted JSON to its internal resume shape; shared ACPX compatibility metadata passes through codecs, while vendor-specific error classifiers inspect stdout/stderr strings.
units.keyDataModels: Vendor session id, working directory, prompt bundle, ACP runtime/session/agent ids, session key/mode/state directory, config fingerprint, workspace/repository/remote lease references and raw process output.
units.lifecycle: Legacy snake_case and vendor-specific fields normalize to a common local shape. ACP lanes round-trip extended resume metadata. Display IDs prefer a runtime or vendor session id. Codex, OpenCode, Cursor and Gemini classifiers recognize missing-session text so orchestration can abandon resume and start fresh.
units.testAssessment: Thirteen focused cases cover five vendor codecs, ACP compatibility preservation and positive/negative error classification. Missing are malformed/untrusted JSON, schema version migration, tenant and Connector-instance binding, path validation, secret stripping, maximum size, unknown-field policy, encrypted persistence, expired/revoked leases, false-positive multilingual/provider changes and structured error codes from adapters.
units.designRationale: Contain unstable vendor session formats behind Adapter-owned codecs while retaining enough opaque runtime state to resume work and recover automatically when an upstream session disappears.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs resumable multi-vendor execution without storing provider-private sessions, credentials or reasoning in its neutral control-plane contract and without coupling recovery to English error prose.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE ONLY for the vendor codecs themselves: they belong inside each Connector and must not enter Company OS Core/Application. Adopt only a versioned opaque SessionRef contract containing connector instance, external opaque id, scope, expiry and attestation digest. Connectors should return structured SESSION_NOT_FOUND/SESSION_UNRECOVERABLE codes and independently migrate encrypted private state.
units.responsibilityConflict: Persisted cwd, repository, state-directory and lease metadata can disclose or revive access outside an approved Work/Data contract if not bound to tenant, Connector instance, authorization version and expiry. Text matching can silently restart a session, risking duplicate effects unless the Work command is idempotent and the restart is audited.

b8fb81dee929f94b7590f33055f55ad472521376 fix(gemini-local): treat token-overflow as a fresh-session signal (#4932)

units.function: Database-backed end-to-end route tests for the Agent/all-actor audit feed, two disclosure tiers, high-precision cursor pagination, filters, safe entity enrichment and permissioned CSV export with export self-auditing.
units.dependencyDirection: Authenticated actor and permission grants select a basic or full audit projection; the route queries Company ActivityLog rows, optionally joins run attribution and visible Issue/comment/document context, serializes cursor/JSON/CSV output and appends an audit.exported activity after export.
units.keyDataModels: Activity actor/action/entity/details, Agent/run/responsible user, Company membership and permission grant, hidden Issue, comment/document projection, microsecond timestamp-plus-UUID cursor, access tier and export receipt.
units.lifecycle: Default Agent-only audit requires explicit permission, while actorScope=all offers a basic redacted feed to Company members and even Agent actors. Basic readers cannot apply attribution/time/entity filters and receive null Agent/run/responsible/details fields. Full readers can filter and receive safe visible-entity enrichment. Cursor pagination preserves sub-millisecond ordering. CSV export escapes spreadsheet formulas and writes a row-count/truncation audit event; denied exports have no export event.
units.testAssessment: Ten substantial integration cases cover authorization order, tiered redaction, all filters, invalid cursors/queries, microsecond pagination, run-attribution fallback, hidden/mismatched entity suppression, CSV injection and export auditing. Missing are immutable/tamper-evident storage, deterministic ordering under identical timestamp/id anomalies, retention/legal hold, very large streaming exports and truncation limits, export purpose/approval, download encryption, actorId pseudonymization, deleted-source history, concurrent inserts, data-classification policy and proof that no sensitive detail leaks through action/entity identifiers or timing.
units.designRationale: Provide a practical, searchable operational audit UI and export while protecting sensitive attribution from ordinary members, preventing hidden-resource disclosure and preserving stable pagination at PostgreSQL timestamp precision.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs both a broad operational activity view and a narrowly governed, exportable responsibility/evidence ledger that can answer who acted, under which authority, with which data and approval, without leaking identities or hidden business objects.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the precision cursor, validate-before-query discipline, hidden-entity suppression, formula-safe export and self-audited export. Split OperationalAuditProjection from append-only ResponsibilityLedger. Apply purpose- and field-level policy to actorId/action/entity metadata, require explicit export authority plus reason/approval, content-hash export manifests, retention/legal hold and immutable source receipts. Never infer authoritative responsibility from a mutable run row.
units.responsibilityConflict: The full feed's responsible user can be backfilled from current run state rather than the contract effective at action time, and ActivityLog is not shown to be append-only or tamper-evident. Basic all-actor access retains actorType/actorId/action/entity identifiers, potentially exposing humans/plugins and sensitive workflows to Agent principals. Export records that an export occurred but not the requester's purpose, approval, exact query/hash or downstream custody.
evidence: 68ddd6a7a0aeb5ca20d0dda24593806522c6a72c feat(activity): add two-tier all-actors audit feed (#10831)
71231dfa38681c10cb2a453485ea402a5258ca8b feat(audit): agent audit UI — company page + per-agent tab (#9744)

units.function: Route tests for validating Agent Adapter types and applying Codex-local credential/home isolation defaults during Agent create and update.
units.dependencyDirection: Agent routes validate the requested type against the active server Adapter registry, transform Adapter config, invoke SecretService/env-binding and instructions helpers, then pass normalized configuration to AgentService persistence.
units.keyDataModels: Agent Adapter type/config, environment map, OPENAI_API_KEY, CODEX_HOME, dynamically registered Adapter and per-Company/per-Agent isolated Codex home path.
units.lifecycle: A dynamically registered external Adapter type can create an Agent, while an unregistered arbitrary string is rejected. Keyless Codex Agents do not receive an injected API key or home on create/update. Supplying a per-Agent OpenAI key automatically selects an isolated Company/Agent Codex home. Callers may also explicitly point a Codex Agent at the host user's shared ~/.codex home.
units.testAssessment: Seven focused route cases cover dynamic/unknown types and the main keyless/keyed create/update home behaviors. Missing are proof that plaintext keys are converted to SecretRef before persistence/logging, path traversal/symlink/ownership/mode checks, cross-Company home reuse, concurrent Agent creation, key removal/rotation, non-OpenAI secrets, shared-home authorization warnings, managed-cloud prohibition, audit receipts and actual filesystem/runtime isolation. Extensive mocks mean database and SecretService guarantees are not exercised.
units.designRationale: Keep Adapter validation extensible while preventing an Agent-specific API key from contaminating or reading the host user's Codex login by default; retain a convenience path for local users who intentionally want to reuse their existing Codex authentication.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must let many vendor-neutral Connectors coexist without inheriting a developer's personal credentials, configuration, sessions or filesystem state, and must keep enterprise secrets and execution identities isolated by tenant and Connector instance.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT registry-backed type validation and automatic per-Connector credential-home isolation. Persist only SecretRef bindings, enforce execution-node-owned private directories and verify permissions. REJECT host ~/.codex sharing as a production/default feature; if retained for single-user local development, gate it behind a deployment-profile policy, explicit high-risk acknowledgement, no enterprise data and a visible non-production status.
units.responsibilityConflict: Sharing the host Codex home can cause an Agent to act with a real person's login, private sessions and ambient authority while the control plane attributes work to a different responsible user. The tests accept plaintext OPENAI_API_KEY in route configuration and mock away persistence normalization, so they do not prove credential custody, redaction or accountable approval.

units.function: Cryptographic unit tests for locally minted Agent run JWTs, including run/responsible-user/scope claims, expiry, issuer/audience validation, Company- and instance-derived keys and optional legacy master-secret verification.
units.dependencyDirection: The local runtime token helper reads process-level signing configuration, derives an HMAC key from control-plane instance and Company identifiers, signs Agent/run claims and verifies them before middleware constructs a request actor.
units.keyDataModels: Agent subject, Company, Adapter type, run id, responsible user, skill-test scope, instance id, issuer/audience, issued/expiry times and legacy-fallback policy.
units.lifecycle: Minted tokens default to a one-hour lifetime and are bound by claims and signature to one Company and control-plane instance. Missing signing configuration disables mint/verify. Issuer, audience, expiration, claim tampering and cross-instance use are rejected. A configurable compatibility path accepts tokens signed directly with the shared master secret; it can be disabled while derived-key tokens continue to work.
units.testAssessment: Sixteen focused cryptographic cases cover normal and scoped tokens, missing/fallback secrets, expiry, issuer/audience, Company and instance isolation, tampering, TTL and legacy-floor behavior. Missing are key identifiers/rotation overlap, asymmetric signing or KMS, jti/revocation, not-before/clock skew, algorithm-confusion/invalid JSON/oversize cases, claim schema validation, Agent/run lifecycle revocation, responsible-human status changes and proof that a token cannot cross deployment profile or Connector instance.
units.designRationale: Give local Agent processes short-lived delegated access without database lookup for every signature check, while limiting a shared secret's direct tenant/instance reach and preserving an upgrade path for already issued tokens.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs short-lived, audience-specific runtime attestations that let any Connector act only for an exact Work execution, tenant and approved responsibility/data contract across managed-cloud and local enterprise nodes.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the tenant/instance key separation, narrow run scope and strict issuer/audience/expiry checks. Use a versioned RuntimeAttestation with key id, Connector instance, WorkExecution, ResponsibilityContract version, authorization/data-policy digest, jti and short expiry; support rotation and revocation through IdentityPort/KMS. Do not fall back to a human-login secret or tenant-agnostic master signature in production.
units.responsibilityConflict: responsible_user_id is a signed string captured at mint time, not evidence that the human accepted responsibility or remained authorized. The token omits approval, permission, data contract and evidence-policy versions. Legacy master-secret acceptance weakens both Company and instance isolation and can outlive organizational changes until expiry.

units.function: HTTP middleware tests for converting signed Agent JWTs and hashed Agent API keys into request actors, preserving scoped delegation, rejecting run spoofing/cross-instance tokens and enforcing a responsible-user binding.
units.dependencyDirection: ActorMiddleware verifies bearer credentials, reads Agent/API-key/heartbeat-run rows for compatibility and status context, writes authentication-denial ActivityLog rows, then downstream route authorization consumes the normalized Agent actor and Company scope.
units.keyDataModels: Agent actor/source, signed run/responsible-user/skill-test claims, optional run header, Agent API key hash/revocation/scope/responsible user, heartbeat run attribution and authentication-denial activity.
units.lifecycle: A valid run JWT produces an Agent actor whose signed run id and responsible user are authoritative; skill-test scope survives. A mismatched run header is rejected with a structured code and audited. Legacy claim-less tokens use the run row's responsible user. Cross-instance tokens fail before protected reads/writes. Agent keys inherit their stored responsible-user binding, while keys without one are denied and audited.
units.testAssessment: Seven route-level cases cover signed-claim precedence, scoped delegation, spoof detection/audit, legacy attribution, instance isolation, API-key attribution and fail-closed missing responsibility. Missing are revoked/expired keys, inactive/deleted Agent or human, key scope enforcement, Company/run/Agent row mismatch, changed responsibility after mint, concurrent revocation, board/session ambiguity, token replay, audit-write failure, timing leakage and end-to-end permission/data-policy checks.
units.designRationale: Normalize multiple non-human credential forms into one downstream authorization actor while ensuring caller-supplied headers cannot replace signed run identity and every durable Agent key has a human attribution anchor.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must authenticate technical Agents and then separately prove their current delegated authority, exact Work binding and accountable human before any data read or effectful action.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the signed-claim authority, header mismatch denial/audit, scoped actor projection and fail-closed missing human binding. Add a current authorization check against immutable ResponsibilityContract and WorkExecution versions, active human/Agent/Connector status, permission and data-policy digests, token jti revocation and action-specific scope. Authentication denial audit must use a resilient append-only security sink.
units.responsibilityConflict: The middleware equates a token/API-key responsible-user value with current accountability and does not show acceptance, employment status or contract version checks. A legacy database fallback derives responsibility after the fact, while a still-valid token may continue to name an offboarded or superseded human. Technical authentication alone cannot authorize enterprise data use or high-risk effects.

units.function: Route tests for cross-Company Agent lifecycle/key isolation and the guarded human action that clears an Agent error only when its organization chain is healthy.
units.dependencyDirection: Agent routes first resolve the target Agent, apply resource-hiding Company access checks and action permission decisions, then call AgentService/HeartbeatService; key revocation additionally resolves and matches the key's Agent. Error recovery reads organization-chain health and appends an ActivityLog event after mutation.
units.keyDataModels: Board/Agent actor, Company-scoped Agent, Agent API key and owning Agent id, Agent status/pause state, organization-chain health/reason/guidance and error-cleared audit action.
units.lifecycle: An outsider receives the same Agent-not-found 404 for pause, error clear, key list/create/revoke and no protected mutation runs. A key belonging to another Agent is also hidden and not revoked. Agent principals cannot clear errors. A Board user can clear an error Agent and emits a distinct audit action, but invalid reporting chains and non-error state return 409 without mutation or success audit.
units.testAssessment: Five route cases cover multiple cross-tenant operations, key-to-Agent ownership, principal type, successful recovery audit and two conflict conditions. Missing are real authz middleware/service integration because the authorization module is replaced, explicit permission variants, local_implicit blast radius, anonymous/instance-admin behavior, concurrent status changes, idempotency, active-run cancellation, key list content leakage, audit-write transaction failure, repair evidence and responsibility acceptance after recovery.
units.designRationale: Close resource-existence oracles before sensitive Agent/key operations and prevent operational recovery from bypassing an invalid human/Agent reporting chain, while making successful manual recovery visible in audit history.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must hide tenant resources, bind every credential to the exact Agent/Connector instance and require a valid accountable-human chain before a failed Agent can resume effectful work.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the indistinguishable 404 pattern, deny-before-side-effect order, key ownership check, human-only recovery and organization-chain gate. Model recovery as a versioned command with expected Agent state, remediation reason/evidence, responsible human, optional risk-based approval, active-run disposition and immutable decision/result receipt. Verify the same matrix through the production IdentityPort/authorization adapter rather than mocked route helpers.
units.responsibilityConflict: The clear-error action proves only that a Board actor clicked recovery while the current org chain was syntactically valid. It does not show that the underlying failure was repaired, that the accountable human accepted resumed risk, or that permissions/data contracts and outstanding runs were revalidated. local_implicit access bypasses ordinary Company membership in the test helper.

units.keyDataModels: Agent actor/target, agent_config:read decision and suggest grant, instruction bundle/file, managed compatibility paths, Adapter type/config, paperclipSkillSync desired Skills and replaceAdapterConfig flag.

Adapter switching carries managed instruction and company Skill selections, even with replacement, while explicit same-Adapter replacement removes instruction fields.

Missing are denied write/delete/update cases, cross-Company resources, low-trust/skill-test actors, path/content validation, version conflicts, Secret/PII redaction, reviewer versus editor separation, immutable artifact history, activity audit, failed filesystem-versus-database transaction rollback and production AccessService integration because services are mocked.
units.designRationale: Expose a unified editing API while preserving Agent behavior-affecting configuration through common Adapter changes and allowing a coaching/suggestion Agent to inspect peer instructions without broad Agent-administration authority.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs an independent Web workflow for reviewing and publishing versioned Agent instructions across Connectors without losing policy on provider changes or granting reviewers excessive read/write capability.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the own/peer scope distinction, narrow agent_config:read action, merge-versus-replace semantics and provider-switch preservation. Read/write versioned InstructionBundle Artifacts through a port; separate view, propose, review and publish permissions, apply field/content classification, optimistic versions, approval and immutable provenance. units.responsibilityConflict: A suggest grant can expose the full peer instruction source, which may reveal business logic or embedded sensitive data, and no test proves that suggestion cannot mutate. units.function: Filesystem integration tests for Agent instruction-bundle mode conversion, managed-root derivation, file listing/export filtering and recovery/self-healing when persisted bundle metadata diverges from disk.
units.dependencyDirection: AgentInstructionsService reads Adapter config and process instance/home settings, derives a Company/Agent managed filesystem root, copies or mutates files and returns healed Adapter configuration plus a bundle projection to routes/persistence.
units.keyDataModels: Managed/external bundle mode, root/managed-root/entry-file/file path, Company/Agent/instance identifiers, filtered file listing/export map, healed Adapter config and recovery warnings.
units.lifecycle: Switching external→managed copies eligible files into an instance/Company/Agent root; managed→external creates the requested entry path with prior content. Listings/exports omit OS junk, Node dependencies and Python caches. If config is absent, partial or points at a stale root, an existing managed bundle wins and warnings explain the repair. Later writes/deletes return corrected metadata.
units.testAssessment: Eight useful filesystem cases cover both mode transitions, nested files, common junk filtering, missing/partial/stale metadata, entry recovery and write/delete healing. Missing are symlink/hardlink escape, ../ and absolute entry paths, root ownership/mode, maximum files/bytes/depth, atomic copy/rollback, concurrent writes, malicious encodings, Secret/PII scanning, executable content policy, content hashes/signatures, version history, approval/audit and behavior when both disk and database changed legitimately.
units.designRationale: Make instruction files portable between user-managed workspaces and a predictable Paperclip-owned location while tolerating older/stale configuration and keeping noisy dependency/cache trees out of API payloads.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs reproducible, reviewable instruction artifacts that Connectors can materialize safely without letting arbitrary host filesystem state silently redefine an Agent's effective behavior.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT managed-root isolation, explicit mode conversion, filtered manifests and recovery warnings. Represent an InstructionBundle as a versioned content-addressed Artifact with manifest, provenance, reviewer/approval, size/type policy and atomic publication; materialize it through Connector/Artifact ports into sandbox-owned directories. Treat arbitrary external roots as local-development imports only, resolving symlinks and scanning content before admission. Disk recovery must produce a proposed reconciliation, not silently supersede authoritative metadata.
units.responsibilityConflict: Instruction content can change Agent behavior and tool usage, yet filesystem copies/recovery have no author, approval, hash, effective interval or link to ResponsibilityContract. Preferring disk over stored metadata can silently activate unreviewed instructions, and external directories may expose unrelated code, credentials or personal files.

units.function: Pure domain-helper tests for deciding whether an Agent can be invoked from its Agent-only reporting chain and enumerating descendants invalidated by a terminated manager.
units.dependencyDirection: Agent lifecycle/assignment services provide a Company Agent snapshot to a stateless graph traversal, which returns an invokable flag, stable reason and reporting-chain details without persistence or external dependencies.
units.keyDataModels: Agent id/Company/status/reportsTo, manager chain, invalid-org-chain flag, reason code and affected descendant ids.
units.lifecycle: An otherwise active Agent is blocked when any ancestor is terminated, its manager is missing or the reporting graph cycles. Terminating a root identifies all non-terminated descendants whose chain becomes invalid while excluding terminated descendants and unrelated roots.
units.testAssessment: Three focused graph cases cover terminated ancestry, missing nodes, cycles, descendant enumeration and unrelated roots. Missing are cross-Company manager ids, self-loop explicitly, deep-chain performance/stack safety, duplicate ids, non-active intermediate statuses, simultaneous graph updates, mixed human/Agent principals, project responsibility, accepted delegation and reason stability across schema versions.
units.designRationale: Prevent Agents from receiving new assignments or runs when the modeled management hierarchy cannot supply a valid supervisory chain, and surface deterministic repair reasons.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must guarantee every executable Agent role reaches an active accountable human through valid organization/responsibility relations before work is authorized.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the pure cycle/missing/terminated graph validation and affected-descendant calculation. Generalize the graph to typed Human/Agent positions and ResponsibilityContracts, require termination at an active accountable human, scope every edge by Company and effective interval, version the graph snapshot used for authorization and emit remediation projections without conflating structure with accepted responsibility.
units.responsibilityConflict: An Agent-only chain can be structurally valid while never naming a real accountable human. reportsTo is treated as sufficient authority without role occupancy, acceptance, effective dates, delegation scope or evidence that the hierarchy snapshot remained valid when a run began.

units.function: Route tests for compact Issue active-run polling, live status/log polling, bounded Company live-run lists with optional recent padding and backward-compatible manual heartbeat wakeup payloads.
units.dependencyDirection: Agent routes resolve Issue/Agent and query HeartbeatService summaries or narrow log access metadata, decorate/redact live status, query bounded run rows directly for Company projections and forward manual invoke fields to HeartbeatService.wakeup.
units.keyDataModels: Issue execution/assignee run, compact Run summary, ephemeral status/tool/snippet/event time, log store/ref/offset, liveness/output-silence fields, list limit/minCount and wake reason/payload/requesting actor/context snapshot.
units.lifecycle: Issue polling returns a compact matching run and ignores a stale foreign-Issue execution pointer by falling back to the assignee's matching run. Ephemeral status fields can be added. Log polling resolves only access metadata before reading a bounded chunk. Company lists default/cap at 50 and query recent completed runs only when minCount is requested. Legacy invoke forwards supplied scope/fresh-session fields or preserves the original minimal empty-body shape.
units.testAssessment: Ten route cases cover compact redaction, stale-pointer recovery, live status, narrow log lookup, caps/defaults, optional padding and two invoke shapes. Missing are real authorization/cross-tenant denial, redaction effectiveness because the registry mock returns input, log limit/offset validation, snippet/tool data classification, cursor pagination, N+1 cost of per-run output-silence decoration, concurrent status changes, WebSocket/event delivery, wake idempotency/replay, risk approval, Work/contract binding and stable structured error behavior.
units.designRationale: Keep high-frequency UI polling lightweight and compatible with older clients while surfacing enough transient execution detail to explain what an Agent is doing and avoiding accidental inclusion of full run context/results.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs safe real-time Agent Boss projections and event streams that show progress/blocking without exposing private reasoning, Secrets or raw enterprise data, and must start work through an idempotent accountable command.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT compact allowlisted projections, exact Issue/run matching, bounded list queries and narrow log metadata access. Classify/redact every ephemeral field, use cursor/event sequence with policy-versioned projections and separate raw-log permission. REJECT the legacy heartbeat invoke shape as canonical: WorkExecution start must require idempotency key, Goal/Work, Connector instance, ResponsibilityContract, permission/data-policy digests and risk/approval context.
units.responsibilityConflict: currentStatusMessage, lastAssistantSnippet, tool name and raw log chunks can leak source data or private reasoning without shown field policy. Manual wakeup names a requester but not the accountable human/approved Work or idempotency receipt; empty-body retries can create duplicate effects and arbitrary payload fields are not an authorization contract.

units.function: Large route-level authorization suite spanning Agent read/config redaction, updates, host commands and instruction paths, Agent creation/hiring/approval/termination, runtime defaults, environment compatibility, task-assignment grants, peer configuration, Agent inbox and heartbeat cancellation.
units.dependencyDirection: Agent routes combine authenticated actor and AccessService decisions with Agent/Approval/Heartbeat/Environment/Secret/Instruction/Skill/Budget services, normalize configuration, persist Agent/membership/grant state and emit ActivityLog/telemetry. Tests mock nearly every service but exercise the real Express route branching.
units.keyDataModels: Board/Agent actor and Company scope, Agent adapter/runtime/permissions/trust/status, SecretRef env, host workspace command, InstructionBundle path, Agent membership/grants, hire Approval, heartbeat/model-profile defaults, instance Environment/driver, task-assignment source, peer configuration and user inbox filter.
units.lifecycle: Read-only members receive empty adapter/runtime config while privileged Board views retain full config. Unauthorized members cannot update, create keys or wake Agents. Agent self-service cannot set host commands or instruction roots, including nested cheap profiles and hires; Board administrators can. Direct creation requires agents:create and is disabled when Company hire approval is required, creates membership plus tasks:assign, disables timer/cheap profiles by default and tolerates optional model-profile discovery failure. Pending Agents can be approved directly or through a linked approval; termination resolves linked approval and cancels invocations. Environment drivers are checked against Adapter capability, including instance-scoped cross-Company environments. Permission updates preserve omitted Skill denial but couple Agent creation to task assignment. Peer config reads require suggest/configure grants; cross-tenant Agent/run operations return 404.
units.testAssessment: Forty-plus route cases provide unusually broad regression coverage for sensitive branches, nested command denial, Secret normalization, approval double-apply avoidance, environment/Adapter compatibility, cross-tenant hiding and patch preservation. Missing are production AccessService/database/transaction integration, denial side-effect assertions on every branch, immutable decision receipts, optimistic concurrency, requester-versus-approver separation, Secret redaction even for admins, command allowlisting/sandboxing, revoke/session propagation, risk/data policy, user inbox delegation binding, scoped peer resource checks, environment trust and rollback across Agent/grant/instruction/approval writes. The suite explicitly demonstrates raw API-key return to a privileged Board actor and arbitrary userId in Agent inbox lookup.
units.designRationale: Centralize a complex compatibility surface while preventing Agent self-escalation into host code/filesystem control, supporting simple-mode usability, optional enterprise approval and multiple local/remote runtimes without breaking older configurations.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs action-specific, tenant- and resource-scoped authorization that separates human viewing, proposing, approving and executing; no convenience mode may bypass Secret custody, accountable delegation or data-purpose boundaries.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT nested dangerous-config detection, read-versus-admin projections, explicit create permission, approval-linked idempotent activation/termination, timer-off defaults, environment capability checks, tri-state patches and cross-tenant 404. REJECT raw Secret values in any config response, arbitrary Board-authored host commands without code-package trust/approval, direct self-approval, simple-mode task assignment and canCreateAgents=>tasks:assign coupling. Bind inbox access to signed delegated-human scope, not a query userId. Split the monolithic route into commands with PolicyPort decisions and immutable receipts.
units.responsibilityConflict: A privileged Board response can contain PAPERCLIP_API_KEY plaintext. A Board actor can configure host-executed commands and directly approve a pending Agent without demonstrated separation of duties. Newly created/active Agents receive task assignment broadly, expanding delegation without a ResponsibilityContract. An Agent can request another user's inbox view by userId without a signed on-behalf-of binding. Peer suggest access is decided at Company resource scope rather than the exact target Agent/config fields.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres end-to-end tests for run-bound Agent Secret metadata/value access, binding resolution, success auditing, runtime log-redaction registration and denial of low-trust/special-scope callers.
units.dependencyDirection: An Agent actor and heartbeat run enter Secret routes; SecretService resolves Agent and run-snapshotted Project bindings, decrypts a local-encrypted version, registers the returned value with the run redaction registry, writes SecretAccessEvent/ActivityLog records and returns metadata or plaintext value.
units.keyDataModels: Company Secret/provider/version, target binding/config path/projection class, Agent/run/key scope, run context manifest and redaction fingerprint/material, SecretAccessEvent and ActivityLog.
units.lifecycle: Listing returns only bound Agent plus run-manifest Project Secret metadata and emits no value-access event. Fetching a bound value returns key/value/version with no-store, first persists a redaction registration without embedding plaintext in the run snapshot, then records success. Concurrent identical registrations deduplicate. Persistence failure rejects delivery. Unbound values are denied. Low-trust review, task-bridge and skill-test callers cannot list or fetch.
units.testAssessment: Four strong database cases cover multiple binding layers, metadata-only listing, plaintext non-leak assertions, success audit, fail-closed redaction, concurrency deduplication and three restricted caller classes. Missing are cross-Company/run/Agent mismatches, revoked/rotated Secret versions, provider outage, lease/TTL/single-use delivery, response/body/log proxy leakage, memory zeroization, denial audit for unbound requests, purpose and data-export policy, high-risk approval, rate limiting, concurrent rotation, KMS/HSM and proof that redaction material itself is encrypted and access-controlled.
units.designRationale: Allow a running Agent to discover only assigned Secrets and fetch values when necessary, while registering exact redaction material before release so subsequent logs can be scrubbed and denying less trusted execution lanes entirely.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs Secret delivery that is tenant-, Work-, Connector-, purpose- and data-policy-bound, keeps values out of the control-plane domain where possible and leaves a complete custody/access record.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT binding resolution, metadata/value separation, no-store, redaction-before-delivery, failure closure, run snapshot manifest and low-trust denial. Prefer execution-node injection or short-lived broker leases over plaintext control-plane API responses; bind every access to WorkExecution, ResponsibilityContract, purpose and export policy, use provider/version references, expiry and least-use scope, and audit allowed plus denied attempts without revealing Secret existence.
units.responsibilityConflict: A successful fetch is linked to Agent/run but not to an accountable human, exact permission/data contract or approval. Plaintext crosses the HTTP/control-plane boundary. An unbound Secret request is denied without a SecretAccessEvent or ActivityLog entry, leaving attempted access outside the responsibility record even if existence-hiding is desired.

units.function: Pure helper tests for normalized Agent display-name collision detection and automatic numeric suffix selection.
units.dependencyDirection: AgentService passes an in-memory Agent name/status set to shortname normalization helpers before create/update naming; no database constraint or external dependency is involved.
units.keyDataModels: Agent id/name/status, normalized shortname, excluded Agent id and generated numeric suffix.
units.lifecycle: Active Agents collide after normalization, the Agent being updated is excluded, names with no normalized shortname do not collide and terminated Agents are ignored. Deduplication retains the original name or appends/increments a suffix until the snapshot appears unique.
units.testAssessment: Eight small cases cover normalization, termination, self-exclusion, empty normalized names and suffix progression. units.testAssessment: Thirty substantial route cases cover Claude/Codex/ACPX/persistent modes, Secret-resolution options, explicit merge semantics, version gating, stale references, canonicalization, direct create, telemetry role, instruction defaults, legacy rejection and hire approval/source preservation. units.designRationale: Separate desired Skill selection from runtime representation, avoid side effects during reads, preserve backward-compatible stale choices, make destructive replacement explicit and keep Agent creation/approval configuration stable across multiple Adapter ecosystems.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a vendor-neutral Skill/Plugin lifecycle where desired capability, reviewed package version, Connector materialization and effective runtime authority are distinct, auditable states tied to accountable humans and data policy.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT side-effect-free list/sync preparation, explicit add/remove/replace, canonical references, unresolved-item quarantine, Secret-safe audit context and approval configuration snapshots. Move desired Skills out of vendor Adapter config into a versioned CapabilityAssignment aggregate. units.function: Route tests for running Adapter environment diagnostics on the explicitly selected sandbox/remote target, managing test leases and merging Environment Secret/plain variables with Agent config.
units.dependencyDirection: The route authorizes Company Adapter configuration, resolves Environment and Secret bindings, acquires/realizes a fresh execution lease, resolves an Adapter execution target, invokes Adapter.testEnvironment with merged config and always releases the driver lease with released/failed status.
units.keyDataModels: Company Environment/driver/config/envVars, SecretRef/missing binding, execution lease/workspace/target, Adapter config env, diagnostic check/status and sandbox/provider/snapshot identity detail.
units.lifecycle: Missing or unsupported requested environments return structured diagnostics without host probing. A supported target uses a fresh non-reused lease with custom image, archives it on release and reports sandbox identity. Workspace failure marks/releases the lease failed. Environment env is the base layer, Agent env wins, protected PAPERCLIP_API_KEY is filtered, and missing Secret bindings add failure checks; however the Adapter probe still runs with remaining variables when a binding is missing.
units.testAssessment: Seven route cases cover the critical no-host-fallback invariant, missing target, happy-path lease identity/release, realization failure, env precedence/protected key filtering and missing-binding diagnostics. Missing are real authorization denials, cross-Company environment id, probe timeout/cancel/network policy, malicious Adapter output, lease cleanup failure, archive retention/privacy, Secret redaction in diagnostic/error/logs, Agent override of protected environment policy, idempotency/rate limits and a fail-before-execute assertion for missing required Secrets.
units.designRationale: Make configuration tests reflect the environment where work will actually run, keep failed sandboxes inspectable and prevent misleading success from probing the control-plane host instead of an unsupported remote target.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a safe Connector/Environment certification probe that never escapes to the host, never runs with an incomplete authority set and produces a structured, attributable health attestation for managed-cloud and local enterprise nodes.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT explicit-target/no-host-fallback, fresh lease, structured diagnostics, protected control-plane keys and release-on-all-paths. Resolve and validate all required Secret/data bindings before executing any probe; apply an allowlisted env merge where policy-owned keys cannot be overridden by Agent config. Run probes in an isolated, egress-limited disposable sandbox and return a signed short-lived HealthAttestation. Archive only after explicit diagnostic-retention policy and Secret scrubbing.
units.responsibilityConflict: A missing required Secret still permits partial probe execution, which can create effects under a different authority set than the approved runtime. Agent config wins env conflicts without shown policy classification. The test action has no accountable requester/approval/audit receipt, and archived failed sandboxes may retain enterprise data or credentials.

units.function: Database integration test proving pending-hire Agent configuration is service-frozen and activation reapplies the approved configuration snapshot even after direct Agent-row tampering.
units.dependencyDirection: AgentService creates/freeze-checks the pending Agent; ApprovalService stores the requested payload and, on approval, applies that payload back through Agent activation and related budget/config persistence.
units.keyDataModels: Pending Agent identity/role/config/runtime/budget/metadata/permissions, hire Approval requester/decision/payload and activated Agent state.
units.lifecycle: Generic Agent and permission updates on a pending Agent return a structured 409 listing frozen fields. Even a direct database change to name/config/runtime/metadata is overwritten when the Approval is approved, restoring the request snapshot and activating the Agent.
units.testAssessment: One high-value integration case covers service mutation denial, permission denial, deliberate database tamper and full snapshot reapplication. Missing are tampering with the Approval payload itself, cryptographic snapshot digest, concurrent decisions, requester/approver separation, partial apply/rollback, Secret version changes, environment/package availability drift, rejection/expiry/cancel and audit evidence linking the exact approved bytes to activation.
units.designRationale: Close the approval-time-of-check/time-of-use gap so an approved hire cannot activate with configuration changed after the reviewer inspected it.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS requires every high-risk approval to bind the exact action/configuration digest and reject or re-review any drift before execution or Agent activation.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT frozen pending state and snapshot reapplication. Store an immutable canonical request digest plus referenced Instruction/Skill/Secret-policy/Connector versions, sign or hash-chain the decision receipt, enforce requester/approver separation by risk and revalidate dependencies at activation. Any drift creates a new approval revision rather than silently reapplying mutable JSON.
units.responsibilityConflict: The same board-user requests and approves in the fixture, and the mutable Approval payload is treated as authoritative without content digest or independent evidence. Restoring config protects Agent-row tampering but cannot prove the reviewer saw the exact activated external package, Secret version or data policy.
