units.testAssessment: Eleven strong integration cases cover terminal/live/mixed locks, idempotency, missing processes, reuse-lease terminal Issues, shared-run safety including misleading context snapshot, and post-terminalization audit failure. Missing cases include cross-company references, two sweepers racing, PID reuse, remote/container execution where host PID is meaningless, lease expiry/fencing token, transaction crash points, audit repair and Connector-signed termination receipts.
units.designRationale: Repair durable execution state after process teardown paths fail, while avoiding terminalizing a run still referenced by active work.
units.companyOsProblem: Managed-cloud and self-hosted Company OS need fenced execution leases, crash recovery and proof that a Connector run is gone before releasing authority or scheduling a replacement.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the shared-reference safety cases, idempotent sweep and explicit unknown-outcome terminal status. Replace host-PID authority with versioned ExecutionLease plus Connector heartbeat/attestation and compare-and-set fencing; make terminal event and audit/outbox atomic or add a tested repair projection.
units.responsibilityConflict: The sweeper can infer success solely because an Issue is done and can proceed when the audit event fails. Company OS must not turn mutable task status into execution proof or lose the evidence/authority receipt that explains who or what terminalized the run.
evidence: f3db7b88 Clear stale checkoutRunId on run finalization and add backstop sweeper (#6008)

units.function: Pure policy tests for bounded plan-only/empty-response continuation and guard conditions.
units.dependencyDirection: Vitest imports the compatibility barrel; fixtures cast partial DB rows to never.
units.keyDataModels: Source run, issue assignment/execution state, Agent status, budget block, attempt and wake payload.
units.lifecycle: Evaluate first/second retry, exhaustion and guarded skip cases.
units.testAssessment: Covers two-attempt bound, idempotency key shape, reassignment, terminal issue, execution policy, paused Agent, budget and existing wake. It does not cover concurrency against the DB, responsible-human continuity, action/data contract, cancellation, timeout or malicious nextAction text.
units.designRationale: Prevent endless automatic loops after non-progressing runs.
units.companyOsProblem: Recovery must be bounded, idempotent and subordinate to responsibility/risk policy.
units.companyOsFit: Adapt the bounded-attempt and reassignment/budget guards after auditing the canonical recovery module; add exact contract digest and Connector capability assertions.
units.responsibilityConflict: The continuation payload carries instructions but no immutable work/responsibility/approval/data digest, so a resumed execution is not proven equivalent to the original authority.

units.function: Unit corpus for Paperclip's regex/evidence-based liveness classifier.
units.dependencyDirection: Vitest imports the pure classifier with literal run/issue/output fixtures.
units.keyDataModels: Run state, output text, evidence counts, actionability and next action.
units.lifecycle: Supply representative English output and compare one classification.
units.testAssessment: Good regression coverage for known cases, including preferring durable comments over dangerous transcript text. It lacks multilingual/adversarial/property tests and validates regex outcomes rather than an authoritative protocol.
units.designRationale: Keep automatic retries stable as textual Agent behavior evolves.
units.companyOsProblem: Fallback heuristics need a falsification corpus and must never silently become policy.
units.companyOsFit: Borrow adversarial transcript-precedence cases for a non-authoritative fallback suite; add explicit confidence/source labels and prove security decisions ignore this output.
units.responsibilityConflict: The test named 'keeps approval requests out' may suggest a security guarantee it cannot provide against rephrasing or non-English output.

units.function: Pure executable specification for task-subtree liveness, material stop fingerprints, reviewed-state suppression and the first-run race window.
units.dependencyDirection: Imports only the exported classifier/type from task-watchdogs and supplies in-memory Issue/path/wait fixtures.
units.keyDataModels: Classifier Issue tree, live run/wake paths, blocker and wait IDs, v2 material stop snapshot, reviewed fingerprint/snapshot and first-run timing inputs.
units.lifecycle: Build tree snapshots; classify live/stopped/pending/already-reviewed; compare fingerprints after metadata, leaf, assignee, blocker and wait changes; exclude watchdog-origin subtrees.
units.testAssessment: Fifteen named tests plus five material-change table cases give strong deterministic policy coverage. Gaps include cycles, depth/size bounds, duplicate IDs, invalid dates, tenant-mixed parents, ordering/property tests, human waits and approval/data-contract semantics.
units.designRationale: Keep noise-suppression and race-handling semantics independent of database orchestration.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs pure, replayable liveness and intervention policy tests with stable versioned outputs.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE the table-driven material-change and race-window scenarios; add property tests, responsibility and authorization waits, and explicit policy-version migration fixtures.
units.responsibilityConflict: The classifier treats pending approvals as fingerprint material but does not decide which human owns the wait or whether an Agent may act around it.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres integration specification for watchdog reconciliation, reusable review Issues, wake idempotency/context, reviewed snapshots, stale review recovery and mutation-fingerprint revalidation.
units.dependencyDirection: Invokes taskWatchdogService against real Paperclip schema and captures a fake wake adapter, spanning Issues, Runs, Wake requests, Approvals, Interactions, Documents, Work Products, comments and activity logs.
units.keyDataModels: Company, Agent, Issue tree, IssueWatchdog, HeartbeatRun, AgentWakeupRequest, pending approval/interaction, evidence timestamps, stop snapshots and activity records.
units.lifecycle: Seed watchdogs and tree state; reconcile; inspect created/reopened review Issue, snapshots, comments and wake context; change live/material/review state; reconcile again; verify suppression, re-trigger or stale-scope denial.
units.testAssessment: Eighteen integration cases cover initial trigger, duplicate suppression, stale review, Run/Wakeup live paths, nested exclusion, ancestor reconciliation, reviewed snapshot reuse and JSON round-trip, old/new fingerprint ordering, evidence-only changes, wait payloads, create-race, true idle work and recursion prevention. It does not inject failures between sequential writes, run concurrent reconcilers, verify durable wake uniqueness in the database, test large/deep trees or assert human authority and Connector evidence receipts.
units.designRationale: Protect the cross-table invariants that the pure classifier alone cannot prove.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs intervention compatibility tests spanning event replay, incident projection, authorization, notification and recovery across managed and local profiles.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE the scenario catalog but implement against Company OS public ports/events and transactional outbox, including crash matrices and multi-node races.
units.responsibilityConflict: The scheduler proves an Agent wake, not accountable-human acknowledgement or approval; its success criteria omit immutable responsibility and data authorization receipts.

units.function: Mints and verifies short-lived HS256 Agent run tokens bound to company, control-plane instance, adapter, run and optional responsible user/scope.
units.dependencyDirection: Server auth adapter depends on process secrets/shared scope normalization; middleware consumes neutralized claims, but vendor adapter type remains in token claims.
units.keyDataModels: sub/company_id/adapter_type/run_id/responsible_user_id/key_scope/iat/exp/iss/aud/instance_id/jti claims and per-instance/per-company derived HMAC key.
units.lifecycle: Derive scoped signing key, mint token, verify signature/current-or-legacy key, parse claims, check expiry and conditional issuer/audience/instance, then create Agent actor.
units.testAssessment: 17 JWT tests and seven middleware tests cover signing, expiry, tenant/instance isolation, legacy fallback, run/header mismatch and responsible-user behavior. Gaps: custom JWT implementation, no maximum TTL/future-iat check, no replay/jti store, optional iss/aud/instance acceptance for legacy tokens, shared-secret rotation and a legacy raw-secret forgery window.
units.designRationale: Issue runtime-local credentials without storing raw provider sessions and harden fork/company isolation after a documented incident.
units.companyOsProblem: Connectors need short-lived secret-free runtime proof bound to exact work, capability, tenant and accountable human.
units.companyOsFit: Tenant/instance key separation and run/responsible-user binding are valuable. Company OS should use a standard signed-token library or asymmetric workload identity, mandatory issuer/audience/instance/action digest, bounded clock skew/TTL, key IDs/rotation and replay policy through Identity/Execution ports.
units.responsibilityConflict: A responsible_user_id claim is only identity context, not proof that the human approved the exact action, permissions, data grant or result.

units.function: Express composition root mounting every HTTP route, authentication/host/CSRF middleware, plugin host, UI, schedulers and background exporters.
units.dependencyDirection: A 752-line outer composition root imports virtually every route and plugin service plus static/Vite UI; inward modules do not import it.
units.keyDataModels: App options, deployment exposure, plugin lifecycle handles, host-service disposers and startup promises.
units.lifecycle: Configure parsing/logging/host/auth guards, mount routes, construct plugin/event/tool services, serve UI, start jobs/watchers/exporters and register cleanup.
units.testAssessment: Many route and app integration tests cover individual behavior, hostname gating and authorization. There is no concise composition-contract test proving route-by-route auth/size/origin policy; correctness is distributed across mount order and each router.
units.designRationale: Centralize startup wiring and keep route/service implementations independently testable.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a narrow API service entry with consistent identity, authorization, size, idempotency and audit policies.
units.companyOsFit: Explicit composition is useful, but this root owns too many domains and background lifecycles. Company OS should compose bounded modules through uniform policy middleware and generated route metadata rather than rely on a long hand-ordered mount list.
units.responsibilityConflict: A route mounted outside the expected guard order can bypass organizational responsibility policy. Responsibility checks must be application invariants, not only Express topology.

units.function: Better Auth integration for email/password sessions, instance-scoped cookies, trusted origins and rate limiting.
units.dependencyDirection: Outer identity adapter depends on better-auth/Drizzle and Paperclip auth tables/config; middleware resolves its session shape.
units.keyDataModels: User/session/account/verification rows, session result, cookie prefix, base URL/trusted origins and rate-limit options.
units.lifecycle: Create auth instance against DB schema, issue session cookies, resolve sessions from request headers and map to board actor.
units.testAssessment: 17 focused Better Auth tests plus auth route/session tests cover cookie isolation, secure-cookie choices, trusted origins and rate-limit defaults. Email verification is disabled, sign-up defaults enabled, and enterprise OIDC/SAML/LDAP lifecycle is not represented.
units.designRationale: Provide a simple embedded identity system for local/self-hosted and authenticated modes.
units.companyOsProblem: Managed cloud and local enterprise need replaceable IdentityPort adapters with isolated token audience, tenant binding and independent audit.
units.companyOsFit: Cookie-instance isolation and origin derivation are useful references. Better Auth may be one adapter, never core; production profiles need explicit enrollment, verified identities and enterprise federation/provisioning/deprovisioning contracts.
units.responsibilityConflict: Authentication proves a principal session, not company role, accountable-human assignment or action approval; those remain Company OS domain checks.

units.function: Reads and validates the persisted JSON configuration with a shared Zod schema while warning about likely misspelled keys.
units.dependencyDirection: Server file adapter depends on shared config schema and local home-path resolution; domain code does not call it directly.
units.keyDataModels: Versionless PaperclipConfig JSON plus unknown-key suggestion warnings.
units.lifecycle: Resolve path, read/parse JSON, schema-validate, emit suggestions, return typed config or fail startup.
units.testAssessment: Focused config-file tests cover invalid JSON/schema and unknown-key preservation. They do not establish versioned migrations, atomic writes, rollback, provenance or concurrent writer behavior.
units.designRationale: Fail early on malformed operator configuration without deleting forward-compatible unknown keys.
units.companyOsProblem: Managed-cloud and self-hosted profiles need validated, evolvable, supportable configuration with FDE overlays.
units.companyOsFit: Schema validation and preservation of unknown keys are useful. Company OS additionally needs explicit config schema versions, source precedence/provenance, secret-free support export and transactional migration/rollback.
units.responsibilityConflict: Configuration can change execution and security policy; consequential changes need an actor, digest and audit receipt rather than an anonymous file mutation.

units.function: Combines env, JSON config, defaults, path resolution and bind-mode detection into the runtime server configuration.
units.dependencyDirection: Outer startup adapter depends on shared deployment enums and host filesystem/process commands; config values then fan into every service.
units.keyDataModels: Deployment mode/exposure/bind, auth origin, database/backup, secrets, storage, feedback export, scheduler, deletion and telemetry settings.
units.lifecycle: Load dotenv and file config, apply env precedence/defaults, optionally detect Tailscale, validate bind constraints and return one config object.
units.testAssessment: Configuration behavior is exercised indirectly and through bind/environment tests. Important env parsing is not uniformly strict: unknown enum values silently fall back, most booleans treat any non-'true' value as false, and numeric values use coercion/defaults. This can conceal operator mistakes.
units.designRationale: Offer zero-config local startup and flexible env overrides for containers and managed deployments.
units.companyOsProblem: Dual deployment profiles need the same business code but different adapters and enforceable security posture.
units.companyOsFit: The unified profile object and bind validation are useful. Company OS must parse every security-relevant env value strictly, reject invalid/unknown inputs, expose effective redacted config with provenance, and separate managed policy from mutable local preferences.
units.responsibilityConflict: Silent fallback can weaken intended identity, secret or exposure policy without a visible accountable decision.

units.function: Recognizes Postgres unique violations across Drizzle/driver cause chains and optional constraint names.
units.dependencyDirection: Server service helper depends only on error shapes/SQLSTATE and is called by transactional workflows.
units.keyDataModels: SQLSTATE 23505, constraint/constraint_name and bounded cause chain.
units.lifecycle: Walk up to four causes, detect unique violation and optional exact constraint, return boolean.
units.testAssessment: Focused tests cover wrapped driver variants, names/messages and unrelated failures. The bounded walk is deterministic and does not leak SQL text.
units.designRationale: Translate driver-specific wrapped conflicts into domain-level deduplication behavior.
units.companyOsProblem: Idempotent Connector/work/approval operations need portable conflict recognition at storage adapters.
units.companyOsFit: The cause-chain technique is useful inside a Postgres adapter, but Company OS application code should receive a neutral storage conflict code.
units.responsibilityConflict: None if kept in the storage adapter; a uniqueness conflict must not be interpreted as proof that the same human-approved action succeeded without digest comparison.

units.function: Minimal HTTP exception type and status-specific constructors.
units.dependencyDirection: Routes/services throw the server-specific HttpError; error middleware serializes it.
units.keyDataModels: HTTP status, English message and optional untyped details.
units.lifecycle: Construct error in service/route, propagate through Express, serialize message/details.
units.testAssessment: Behavior is covered through route/error-handler tests, but the type does not require a stable code, structured parameters, audience, retryability or safe/public distinction.
units.designRationale: Keep route errors concise and compatible with Express.
units.companyOsProblem: Independent Web, Connector SDK and future bilingual UI require stable machine contracts rather than English text matching.
units.companyOsFit: The status helpers are too weak. Company OS needs mandatory stable code, safe structured parameters, correlation ID, retry class and internal/public cause separation.
units.responsibilityConflict: Free-form details can accidentally expose sensitive evidence or misstate why a responsibility decision was denied.

units.function: Defines default JSON and company-portability upload ceilings, including an environment-overridable compressed ZIP limit.
units.dependencyDirection: Transport constants are imported by app/import routes; no inward domain dependency.
units.keyDataModels: 10 MiB default JSON, 64 MiB portable JSON and a 1 GiB default/64 GiB maximum compressed ZIP byte limit.
units.lifecycle: Parse the environment override at module load, clamp/fallback, configure whole-body parsers and derive decompression guards in import handling.
units.testAssessment: Six focused tests verify constants, override fallback and arithmetic clamping. The code explicitly states the entire upload is buffered in memory and allows up to 64 GiB, but tests do not exercise concurrency, process memory, slow uploads, authenticated tenant quotas or streaming decompression.
units.designRationale: Accept large real-world company packages in one request while bounding decompression arithmetic.
units.companyOsProblem: Enterprise import/export and FDE templates need large portable packages without turning the API into a memory/zip-bomb denial-of-service path.
units.companyOsFit: Separate route-specific limits are sensible, but the in-memory 1–64 GiB design is unacceptable. Company OS should stream to quarantined object storage, enforce compressed/uncompressed/file-count/ratio/tenant quotas, verify digest/signature, scan before activation and resume idempotently.
units.responsibilityConflict: Import mutates organization/data/permission state and needs an accountable initiator, validated manifest digest, preview and explicit apply receipt.

units.function: Full process startup and shutdown: instrumentation, Postgres, migrations, backups, auth, backfills, managed config, adapters, schedulers, WebSockets and listening.
units.dependencyDirection: A 1,536-line process entry imports DB migrations and most server services; it is the terminal composition layer.
units.keyDataModels: StartedServer, migration state, embedded/external DB runtime, deployment/auth state, managed config, backup health and shutdown coordination.
units.lifecycle: Initialize telemetry/secrets, provision DB, inspect/reconcile/apply migrations, validate deployment contracts, backfill/reconcile state, build app and realtime, start schedulers/backups, load adapters, listen, then coordinated shutdown.
units.testAssessment: Startup, shutdown, migration, managed-config, worktree and feedback-export behaviors have focused tests, but the entire production sequence is not exercised as one failure-matrix. Non-interactive startup automatically approves pending migrations unless PAPERCLIP_MIGRATION_PROMPT=never, increasing unattended upgrade risk.
units.designRationale: Make a single command self-healing and easy to operate, including embedded Postgres and compatibility backfills.
units.companyOsProblem: Self-hosted enterprise needs reliable migration, backup, recovery, health, upgrade and rollback semantics.
units.companyOsFit: Refusal to run on stale schema, migration inspection, startup ordering and coordinated cleanup are important references. Company OS should split the orchestrator into testable phases, require an explicit production migration policy, support preflight/backup/rollback receipts and avoid behavior-changing data backfills hidden in process startup.
units.responsibilityConflict: Automatic schema/backfill changes are consequential administrative actions and require operator policy, immutable evidence and rollback ownership.

units.function: Masks current OS usernames and home-directory paths recursively before log export.
units.dependencyDirection: Logging adapter depends on process/env/path data; business records remain untouched.
units.keyDataModels: Candidate usernames/home dirs, replacement token and recursively redacted values.
units.lifecycle: Discover candidate identity strings, replace longest paths then bounded username tokens, recurse plain objects/arrays.
units.testAssessment: Four focused tests cover path, token-boundary, nested and disabled behavior. It cannot discover every PII path or guarantee redaction of non-plain objects/buffers.
units.designRationale: Prevent workstation identity leakage in diagnostic logs while preserving useful paths.
units.companyOsProblem: FDE support bundles and managed-cloud telemetry must not exfiltrate local employee/device identity.
units.companyOsFit: Useful defense-in-depth for support export. Company OS should combine structured sensitivity labels, allowlisted fields and tenant policy; original user input/evidence stays in its governed store rather than being mutated.
units.responsibilityConflict: Redaction must preserve evidence integrity by storing original and redacted derivative separately with a digest/provenance link.

units.function: HTTP actor resolution, cloud trusted headers, CSRF/origin guard, hostname/DNS-rebinding guard, trust-proxy parsing, validation, logging/redaction, compression and error serialization.
units.dependencyDirection: Transport layer depends on DB/shared/services and writes a rich Express actor used by routes; some authorization semantics therefore live in middleware rather than application services.
units.keyDataModels: Board/Agent actor sources, memberships/on-behalf-of snapshot, key scope/run ID, cloud stack identity, trusted host/origin/proxy config and structured HTTP error response.
units.lifecycle: Resolve implicit/session/cloud/API-key/JWT actor, validate host and browser mutation origin, execute route, sanitize logs and serialize errors.
units.testAssessment: Dedicated tests cover Agent auth, 17 cloud-tenant cases, board mutation, private host, trust proxy, errors and redaction. Important issues remain: local_trusted is implicit instance admin; Cloud uses one static trusted-header token; private-host and board-origin code reads X-Forwarded-Host directly rather than only through the configured trusted-proxy interpretation; stable error codes are optional.
units.designRationale: Normalize many transport identities once and provide backwards-compatible on-behalf-of human context to all routes.
units.companyOsProblem: Every request needs tenant/principal/capability context, but responsibility/data authorization must remain uniform across HTTP, events and Connector dispatch.
units.companyOsFit: Fail-closed missing responsible user, active membership snapshots and stale elevation cleanup are strong patterns. Company OS should issue a neutral PrincipalContext from IdentityPort, use short-lived audience-bound service identity, derive forwarded host only from trusted proxy state, and enforce responsibility inside application use cases.
units.responsibilityConflict: onBehalfOfUserId is valuable but still only a delegation context. It must not substitute for an exact responsibility contract and high-risk approval digest.

units.function: Server package manifest, build/test entry points and dependency ownership for the Paperclip control-plane process.
units.dependencyDirection: The server directly imports DB/shared/plugin SDK plus every built-in Agent adapter and many infrastructure vendors, making it both composition root and runtime owner.
units.keyDataModels: No domain data; package scripts, published exports and dependency graph.
units.lifecycle: Build/typecheck/test the server and bundle UI/adapter/plugin artifacts into the distributable package.
units.testAssessment: Vitest configuration and a large server suite exist, but the manifest itself has no dependency-policy or architecture test preventing domain-to-vendor coupling. Several runtime packages use compatible ranges rather than exact pins.
units.designRationale: One deployable server simplifies self-hosted installation and makes built-in adapters available without separate services.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a simple deployable profile while preserving replaceable model, Agent, storage, identity and execution ports.
units.companyOsFit: The single-service packaging is operationally useful for an early self-hosted profile, but Company OS must keep vendor adapters out of inward layers and preferably out of the core server package dependency graph.
units.responsibilityConflict: Directly owning execution vendors in the control-plane package encourages transport credentials and sessions to leak across responsibility boundaries.

units.function: Company event WebSocket subscriptions and one-time authenticated SSH terminal bridging for custom sandbox-image setup.
units.dependencyDirection: Realtime transport bypasses Express middleware and implements separate DB/session/key authorization; terminal path depends on custom-image services, ephemeral session store and ssh2.
units.keyDataModels: Company upgrade context, session/API key identity, event subscription, terminal setup/session token, pinned SSH host hash, resize/input/output frames and connection registry.
units.lifecycle: Intercept HTTP upgrade, independently authorize, bind company subscription or validate a short-lived terminal session, bridge frames/SSH, enforce expiry/heartbeat and clean up sockets/sessions.
units.testAssessment: Three live-event tests and eight terminal tests cover cross-company denial, sessions, query/header token behavior, one-time auth, expiry, host verification and cleanup. Live events accept long-lived Agent API keys in URL query parameters, do not accept scoped run JWTs, and do not repeat Agent status/responsible-human checks from HTTP middleware; query credentials may leak through intermediaries despite application log care.
units.designRationale: Support browser-compatible realtime and interactive setup while keeping terminal connection payloads ephemeral.
units.companyOsProblem: Agent Boss needs realtime projections, while local execution setup may require interactive operator intervention without leaking credentials.
units.companyOsFit: One-time terminal tokens, host-key pinning, expiry and cleanup are good patterns. Company OS should use one shared authorization service for HTTP/WebSocket/events, prohibit long-lived credentials in URLs, use short-lived audience/work-scoped tickets and publish only sanitized projection events with resume cursors.
units.responsibilityConflict: Realtime delivery and terminal transport must not create authority. An interactive human identity and any resulting runtime/config mutation need an exact audited responsibility record.

units.function: Recursively removes credential-shaped fields, command flags, JSON fragments and JWT-shaped values from events/log text.
units.dependencyDirection: Server safety helper imports command redaction from adapter-utils and is used across audit/log/run surfaces.
units.keyDataModels: Secret field-name regex, secret/user-secret/plain bindings, CLI argv rules, JWT pattern and REDACTED marker.
units.lifecycle: Inspect field/type/value, preserve safe secret references, redact secret material and command args, recursively sanitize plain data.
units.testAssessment: Eight core tests plus HTTP/run/comment redaction suites cover nested payloads, flags, bindings, JWTs and audit exceptions. Regex/field-name detection remains inherently incomplete and can both miss novel credentials and over-redact ordinary data.
units.designRationale: Apply one broad defense across heterogeneous Agent/provider payloads without requiring every caller to remember secret fields.
units.companyOsProblem: Control-plane events must exclude credentials/private sessions/reasoning while retaining evidence and original business output in authorized stores.
units.companyOsFit: Reference preservation and structured traversal are strong. Company OS should make sensitivity typed at ingestion and deny unknown payload shapes; heuristic redaction remains a final guard, not the primary security boundary.
units.responsibilityConflict: Redacted audit text cannot replace source evidence. Responsibility records must point to immutable authorized evidence digests and record the redaction transform.

units.function: HTTP workflow for generic approvals, revision/resubmission, comments and mutable links between approvals and issues.
units.dependencyDirection: Express routes orchestrate approval, issue-link, comment, Agent and activity services; several responsibility and side-effect rules exist only in this transport layer.
units.keyDataModels: Approval type/status/payload, requester/decider IDs, free-form note, comments and issue-approval links.
units.lifecycle: Agent or board creates an approval, links issues in separate calls, board approves/rejects/requests revision, requester resubmits and participants comment; links remain editable after resolution.
units.testAssessment: Route tests cover actor-derived requester/decider attribution, cross-company protection, payload redaction and idempotent decision responses. They do not require an exact action digest, approval-authority/risk match, immutable target links, evidence/result binding or atomic creation with issue links. Local mode can attribute a decision to the synthetic string 'board'.
units.designRationale: Provide a flexible board inbox that can accommodate several approval types without a schema per type.
units.companyOsProblem: High-risk work must pause on a versioned action contract and resume only after the matching accountable human approves the exact action, permissions, data, evidence expectations and runtime scope.
units.companyOsFit: Actor-derived attribution, hidden cross-tenant existence and idempotent response shape are useful references. Company OS must put approval invariants in application use cases, require a real human principal and make target/action associations immutable after proposal.
units.responsibilityConflict: A mutable issue link and arbitrary payload cannot prove who approved which exact work/action/data contract. Redacting comments before persistence also destroys the original evidence rather than storing a governed original plus derivative.

units.function: Shared route authorization helpers for actor type, instance/company access, cross-tenant existence-oracle protection, actor audit fields and secret-consumer context.
units.dependencyDirection: Express route layer consumes the middleware actor and server authorization shadow-mode setting; services do not depend on these helpers, so some security invariants exist only at HTTP call sites.
units.keyDataModels: Board/Agent actor, company membership and viewer role, on-behalf-of responsible user snapshot, actor source/run/key IDs and secret consumer context.
units.lifecycle: Authenticate actor, hide inaccessible resource existence, intersect Agent company scope with an optional responsible-user membership, enforce read/write role, derive audit/secret context, then call a service.
units.testAssessment: The authorization suites cover 19 company-access cases, five secret-context cases and a static route scan preventing known existence-oracle regressions. Gaps: HTTP method is used as the write-risk proxy; static source scanning cannot prove every dynamic path; stable denial codes are inconsistent; shadow mode intentionally permits responsible-user denials; and an Agent whose onBehalfOfUserId is absent skips the human-membership intersection entirely.
units.designRationale: Centralize backwards-compatible company scoping and prevent 403/404 differences from leaking cross-tenant resource existence.
units.companyOsProblem: Every use case must combine tenant, principal, role, responsible human, data grant, work contract and risk-specific approval without leaking object existence.
units.companyOsFit: The indistinguishable not-found pattern, server-derived secret consumer and human/Agent permission intersection are strong references. Company OS must enforce them inside application use cases across every transport, require an accountable human for formal Agent work, remove shadow bypass from production and authorize named actions rather than HTTP verbs.
units.responsibilityConflict: Paperclip treats responsible human context as optional for some JWT/legacy paths and permits a shadow mode. Company OS requires every formal Agent action to resolve an active responsibility contract and exact human owner before execution.

units.function: Company-scoped HTTP API for decision queues, source membership, triage deadlines/snooze and retention archive/keep controls.
units.dependencyDirection: Express routes combine shared validators, route actor state, authorization actions and queue/retention services; authority remains transport-mediated.
units.keyDataModels: Named queue, heterogeneous attention-source reference, triage override, responsible-user attribution and retention state.
units.lifecycle: Board or eligible Agent reads/manages queues, adds readable sources, changes triage metadata and archives/revives attention sidecars.
units.testAssessment: Embedded-Postgres route tests cover idempotent queue creation, actor audit, heterogeneous source visibility, hidden/missing equivalence, seeded queues, concurrent partial triage updates and restricted task-bridge/skill-test credentials. Stable error codes and application-level responsibility enforcement remain inconsistent.
units.designRationale: Give Agents and humans one durable inbox/triage surface over many decision-like source types without moving the source records.
units.companyOsProblem: Agent Boss needs configurable, responsibility-aware work/approval inboxes without duplicating source truth.
units.companyOsFit: The sidecar queue and per-source read check are useful. Company OS should expose one typed Projection API backed by a source registry, stable codes and application authorization; queue mutation must not imply authority to decide the underlying action.
units.responsibilityConflict: The route records on-behalf-of identity but does not require a responsibility contract, and any principal with generic queue-manage authority can reorder organizational attention regardless of accountable role.

units.function: Human-only capture, preview, library, note editing, deletion and full-company JSONL export for decision-training examples.
units.dependencyDirection: HTTP layer exposes the snapshot service directly and relies on board/company/author checks plus activity logging; export serializes every example in memory.
units.keyDataModels: Frozen state snapshot, human notes/history, outcome label, author and JSONL state/label records.
units.lifecycle: A board user previews/captures a decision snapshot, edits only their notes, browses records and can export all company examples or delete their own record.
units.testAssessment: Tests cover human-only writes/reads/exports, author-only mutation, immutable snapshot, audit of reads/exports, no-op notes and strict update shape. They do not test step-up authorization, export data policy/approval, size/streaming, rate limits, purpose consent, redaction breadth or concurrent note updates.
units.designRationale: Turn human decisions into reusable labeled examples while keeping source state frozen and user guidance editable.
units.companyOsProblem: Future Agent Boss training/certification may learn from decisions, but enterprise data cannot silently become a model-training dataset or leave through an unrestricted export.
units.companyOsFit: Do not copy this route. Company OS needs a Data Authorization/Export Firewall use case with explicit purpose, field manifest, preview, accountable exporter, approval, digest, streaming and revocation/retention policy before any training-library feature.
units.responsibilityConflict: Any board user can export snapshots containing issue, comments and run records without a data-owner contract or high-risk approval. Author ownership of notes does not establish consent from people whose data appears in the snapshot.

units.function: Agent-originated proposal and bundle API, board decision/dismissal API, Agent cancellation/readback, statistics and a reviewed attention-archive proposal flow.
units.dependencyDirection: Express routes validate shared Decision effects and call Decision/attention/authorization services; the API is tied to Paperclip issue and board/Agent actor concepts.
units.keyDataModels: Decision title/body/options/input prompts, typed issue effects, origin Agent/run, expiry/idempotency, continuation policy and signed archive manifest.
units.lifecycle: An in-run Agent proposes bounded effects, board lists and decides, executor applies them and optionally wakes the origin Agent; archive proposals snapshot an exact reviewed manifest.
units.testAssessment: Strict schemas bound option/effect/input counts and agent/board routes constrain proposal versus decision roles. Gaps: every board member can decide regardless of approval authority/risk class; local implicit board is not a real human; most validation errors use English strings rather than mandatory stable codes; generic high-risk data/tool/model actions are not represented.
units.designRationale: Expose a compact human-in-the-loop protocol that an Agent can invoke during one run and continue after a board answer.
units.companyOsProblem: Connector-neutral Agents need pause/resume approval APIs while humans need role/risk-matched decision surfaces independent of a particular work-item model.
units.companyOsFit: Bounded typed effects, origin-run requirement, archive manifest review and continuation are strong API references. Company OS must define its own action envelope, stable error contract, real-human approval authority and Connector protocol instead of copying Paperclip routes/types.
units.responsibilityConflict: Board membership is treated as sufficient approval authority and the API does not require a responsibility-contract/action/data/evidence digest.

units.function: Secret-provider SPI with local AES-256-GCM storage, AWS Secrets Manager managed/reference support, health checks, discovery and GCP/Vault metadata-only stubs.
units.dependencyDirection: Server provider adapters implement a shared SecretProviderModule and depend on filesystem/crypto/AWS credentials; service/routes own DB metadata and bindings separately.
units.keyDataModels: Provider descriptor/capabilities, prepared version material/fingerprint, runtime/write context, external/provider version refs, stable provider client errors and health/backup guidance.
units.lifecycle: Validate provider, create/link/version/resolve/rotate/archive material, retain DB metadata/fingerprints and report health; local key comes from env/file, AWS uses default credential chain and recovery-window deletion.
units.testAssessment: Registry/local tests and 18 AWS tests cover capabilities, key permissions, request signing, credential cache, managed/external versions, listing/discovery, error mapping and deletion. GCP/Vault are non-resolving stubs; local key creation/permission is best effort and lacks envelope encryption/rotation; provider tests are largely mocked.
units.designRationale: Separate secret metadata/bindings from storage material and support both easy local operation and cloud vault custody.
units.companyOsProblem: Agent/model/data connectors require scoped credential custody, rotation, audit and local-enterprise vault integration without exposing values to the control plane.
units.companyOsFit: Provider SPI, version fingerprints, external refs, stable client codes and health/backup guidance are strong. Company OS needs owner/purpose/consumer/action-bound access leases, real Vault/China-cloud adapters, envelope/KMS rotation, no value return to browser/control plane, and fail-closed profile policy.
units.responsibilityConflict: Resolving a secret proves technical access, not that its use was authorized for this work/data purpose. Every resolution must be policy-checked and audited against the accountable human and runtime proof.

units.function: Persistence and state transitions for generic approvals, including hire-Agent activation and related post-approval side effects.
units.dependencyDirection: Application service depends directly on Paperclip approval/Agent/company schemas, adapter reconciliation, budget policy and notification hooks.
units.keyDataModels: Generic JSON payload, pending/approved/rejected/revision_requested status, requester/decider/note/timestamps and hire-Agent configuration.
units.lifecycle: Create pending row, compare-and-set a terminal decision, then perform type-specific hire side effects; revision and resubmission are read-then-update transitions.
units.testAssessment: Focused tests cover create/list/get, deduplication, same-decision idempotency and hire-agent behavior. A critical consistency gap remains: approve changes status before hire side effects; if a later side effect fails, retry observes approved and skips those effects permanently. Revision/resubmit updates do not include the prior status in their WHERE clause, so concurrent terminal decisions can be overwritten.
units.designRationale: Keep a small generic approval table while attaching product-specific behavior in one service.
units.companyOsProblem: Approval resolution and effect publication need a crash-safe, replayable saga/outbox with immutable request digest and per-effect receipts.
units.companyOsFit: The compare-and-set terminal transition is a useful primitive, but this implementation must not be reused. Company OS should separate decision receipt from resumable effect execution and preserve every attempt/result under one responsibility record.
units.responsibilityConflict: Status can say approved while the approved organization/runtime change never happened, and the stored record does not bind action, contract, Agent, human, permissions, data, evidence or result digests.

units.function: Durable heterogeneous attention queues, source-level visibility filtering, triage versioning/events and data-backed starter-queue materialization.
units.dependencyDirection: Service directly switches across approvals, decisions, interactions, runs, issues, recovery, join and budget tables and calls authorization/activity services.
units.keyDataModels: Queue/item, sourceKind/sourceId, creator/adder/responsible user, triage version and append-only triage event.
units.lifecycle: Resolve source to an authorization resource, create/list/update queues, add/remove references transactionally, serialize triage writes with advisory locks and seed PR/plan/question queues idempotently.
units.testAssessment: Tests exercise primary mutations, source visibility, idempotent seeding and concurrent triage merging. Missing coverage includes high-cardinality performance, deleted-source reconciliation for non-board readers, all attention kinds and source-switch/schema drift. Listing performs per-queue then per-item authorization queries, creating an N+1 scaling path.
units.designRationale: Keep attention organization orthogonal to underlying domain objects while preserving source-specific authorization.
units.companyOsProblem: One Agent Boss desk must project tasks, approvals, failures and data/security alerts without one giant coupled service.
units.companyOsFit: Adopt the sidecar-reference, visibility-before-disclosure, versioned triage and append-event ideas. Replace the central sourceKind switch with registered projection providers and batched authorization; source IDs stay opaque and source lifecycle emits reconciliation events.
units.responsibilityConflict: responsibleUserId is optional attribution copied at queue mutation time, not the accountable human frozen on the referenced work contract.

units.function: Versioned attention retention, exact reviewed archive manifests, TTL archive, keep/revive controls and durable Agent notification outbox.
units.dependencyDirection: Service consumes attention projections, source authorization, Paperclip source schemas, activity log and a heartbeat notification callback.
units.keyDataModels: Retention/version/archiveVersion, source activity cutoff, archive actor/reason, signed-review manifest entry and notification outbox claim state.
units.lifecycle: Synchronize source activity, increment version on drift, preserve Keep, atomically re-authorize and archive an exact manifest, auto-archive idle entries, claim stale/pending notifications and retry at least once.
units.testAssessment: Focused tests prove TTL archive/revive, Keep exclusion, one notification batch per Agent and all-or-nothing stale-manifest rejection. Gaps include notification backoff/dead-lettering, concurrent worker locking beyond conditional update, retry ceilings, every source origin mapping, manual archive event atomicity and tenant policy overrides.
units.designRationale: Treat attention as a lifecycle-managed projection and make bulk cleanup reviewable rather than silently deleting source data.
units.companyOsProblem: Responsibility/evidence/attention records need explicit lifecycle, legal retention, human-reviewed bulk actions and reliable follow-up.
units.companyOsFit: This is the best Paperclip reference for exact versioned bulk mutation and outbox delivery. Company OS should generalize it to policy-specific retention/legal hold, immutable evidence retention, retry/dead-letter observability and signed actor/action receipts.
units.responsibilityConflict: Archiving hides a projection rather than deleting evidence, which is appropriate, but generic board/source-read authority is not sufficient for evidence retention or legal-hold changes.

units.function: Canonical-JSON HMAC signing for decision specifications plus secure local generation and persistence of an instance signing secret.
units.dependencyDirection: Server crypto/filesystem adapter is called by the Decision service and depends on Paperclip home-path conventions; no neutral signing port exists.
units.keyDataModels: decision-spec-v1 canonical payload, instance-wide 32-byte-or-longer symmetric secret and version-prefixed SHA-256 HMAC.
units.lifecycle: Resolve explicit secret or atomically publish a generated 0600 key under an owned 0700 directory, sign canonical payload and verify with timing-safe comparison.
units.testAssessment: The implementation defends against partial/concurrent local key creation, ownership and permissive modes. It has no key ID, historical verification set, tenant separation, rotation workflow, asymmetric signer/KMS/HSM adapter or algorithm-agility contract.
units.designRationale: Make tampering detectable in zero-config self-hosting without requiring an external key service.
units.companyOsProblem: Action/approval contracts require deployable-profile-neutral signatures, rotation and durable verification after key changes.
units.companyOsFit: Canonicalization, fail-fast key validation and atomic local creation are strong patterns. Company OS should adapt them behind a SignaturePort with kid/algorithm/tenant/purpose, KMS-capable managed adapter and retained verification keys.
units.responsibilityConflict: A valid instance HMAC proves database content was signed by the instance, not which accountable human consented or whether the signed fields cover the full responsibility contract.

units.function: Captures point-in-time Issue/comment/run/workspace/decision snapshots, resolves a likely code commit, persists labeled examples and scrubs snapshots after source-comment deletion.
units.dependencyDirection: Service reads whole Paperclip DB rows across issues, comments, runs, workspaces and three decision systems, then stores untyped JSON snapshots coupled to those schemas.
units.keyDataModels: Snapshot v1 with full issue/comments/runs, cutoff, decision payload/actor/outcome, approximate commit resolution, notes history and retention marker.
units.lifecycle: Resolve decision cutoff, collect rows last updated before it, infer commit, freeze JSON, deduplicate per source/author, update notes history and redact deleted comment bodies.
units.testAssessment: Strong boundary tests cover cutoff inclusivity, exclusion of later comments/runs/workspaces, comment-deletion scrub, issue cascade, commit-resolution label, uniqueness and snapshot immutability. Missing are schema migration, deterministic canonical digest, field allowlisting, secret/PII redaction, evidence/data provenance, concurrent notes CAS and deletion propagation for run/issue fields beyond comments. Full heartbeat-run rows are copied into the training dataset.
units.designRationale: Prevent hindsight leakage by freezing only information believed available at decision time and preserve code context for later learning.
units.companyOsProblem: Training/evaluation datasets need temporal correctness plus data minimization, consent, lineage and reproducibility.
units.companyOsFit: Temporal cutoff, preview-before-freeze, immutable state/editable label and deletion propagation are excellent design references. Reimplement through governed evidence projections and allowlisted snapshot schemas; never copy entire operational rows or infer authorization from temporal availability.
units.responsibilityConflict: The snapshot omits the governing data contract and copies potentially sensitive operational fields. A recursively discovered commit SHA is not evidence that the selected repository state produced the decision.

units.function: Maps decision/retention continuation events onto Paperclip heartbeat wakeup requests and becomes a no-op when that runtime is disabled.
units.dependencyDirection: Thin adapter couples Decision callbacks to heartbeat vocabulary and payloads.
units.keyDataModels: Agent/issue/decision/outcome continuation and batched archive-version notification.
units.lifecycle: At composition time select enabled wakeup or no-op; on event enqueue a typed automation reason and reference-only payload.
units.testAssessment: Two tests cover disabled no-op and exact decision payload mapping. Retention mapping, idempotency, capability negotiation, missing/deleted Agent, delivery receipt and failure classification are not tested here.
units.designRationale: Avoid accepting continuations when the process cannot own heartbeat execution.
units.companyOsProblem: Paused Connector work must resume through a declared capability without embedding vendor sessions or raw human content.
units.companyOsFit: Reference-only payloads and explicit disabled behavior are useful. Company OS needs a Connector Resume port with idempotency/action digest, capability/version check, timeout/cancellation and delivery/result receipts rather than a heartbeat-specific callback.
units.responsibilityConflict: A wakeup references a decision but does not prove the resumed runtime is bound to the same responsibility/action/data contract.

units.function: Signed human-decision engine with target snapshots, typed issue effects, origin/decider authorization intersection, per-effect execution ledger, idempotency, expiry, continuation delivery and crash recovery.
units.dependencyDirection: Application service directly owns Paperclip issue, run, authorization, activity and retention schemas/services; effect types are Paperclip work-item mutations rather than a portable execution contract.
units.keyDataModels: Decision/bundle, signed options and target snapshots, chosen option/input values, effect execution receipt, origin Agent/run/issue, deciding user, continuation marker and archive manifest.
units.lifecycle: Validate origin run and authority, snapshot targets transactionally, sign effect specification, CAS open to decided, re-authorize origin and decider, claim and execute each effect transactionally, persist result/audit, recover running work and deliver Agent continuation at least once.
units.testAssessment: A substantial focused suite covers idempotent creation/decision, tamper rejection, exact archive manifests, lost access, stale targets, double decision, per-effect failure/partial success, crash recovery, continuation and bounded sweeps. Important gaps: the signature includes only decision ID, options and target snapshots—not title/body/inputs/expiry/origin responsible human/responsibility contract/data grants/approval authority/input values/evidence policy. The accountable human is re-read from the mutable run during execution. Effects are sequential rather than an atomic business transaction, failed effects are terminal rather than policy-driven retryable, and recovery reconstructs a generic board actor from membership.
units.designRationale: Turn Agent proposals into bounded, tamper-evident, human-selected issue mutations that survive crashes without executing one effect twice.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a canonical high-risk decision/effect engine that can prove exact human responsibility and safely resume Connector work across cloud/local execution nodes.
units.companyOsFit: This is Paperclip's best reference for decision execution and supersedes its generic Approval design. Company OS should adapt signed immutable manifests, authorization intersection, per-effect receipts, staleness policy, CAS and recovery, while owning neutral action/evidence/data contracts and never importing Paperclip schema/types.
units.responsibilityConflict: The signed payload does not freeze the accountable human, approving authority, permissions/data contract, evidence/result obligations or supplied inputs. A later run-row change can alter the origin human shown in audit, so it cannot serve as Company OS's responsibility proof.

units.function: Process-local, TTL-bound live status projection for a run's phase/message/tool/assistant snippet with heuristic secret redaction.
units.dependencyDirection: In-memory server adapter depends on Paperclip redaction and shared phase enum; UI readers query it through surrounding Heartbeat APIs.
units.keyDataModels: Company/issue/Agent/run scope, phase, sanitized message/tool/snippet and activity timestamps.
units.lifecycle: Set or touch a scoped Map entry, clone on read, reject scope mismatch and clear/sweep after 90 seconds.
units.testAssessment: Six tests cover scoping, redaction/truncation, expiry, touch monotonicity/fallback and sweep. No multi-process consistency, process restart, capacity/eviction, Unicode size, redaction bypass or authorization-call-site test exists.
units.designRationale: Give responsive live UI feedback without turning noisy transient status into durable database state.
units.companyOsProblem: Agent Boss and office entities need transient working/waiting state while durable evidence remains separate.
units.companyOsFit: The ephemeral-versus-durable split, TTL and scope checks are useful. Company OS should expose an Office/Run Projection port with managed-cloud pub/sub or local memory adapter, bounded capacity and typed safe status codes rather than arbitrary Agent text.
units.responsibilityConflict: Sanitized snippets are not evidence and must not enter the responsibility chain; heuristic redaction is defense-in-depth only.

units.function: Extracts/truncates selected adapter result fields, merges a fallback summary and chooses text to post as an Issue comment.
units.dependencyDirection: Pure server helper accepts untyped vendor result JSON; Heartbeat persistence/comment paths call it.
units.keyDataModels: summary/result/message/error, three cost aliases and timeout/stop metadata.
units.lifecycle: Merge missing summary, project allowlisted top-level fields and select summary/result/message for a comment.
units.testAssessment: Eight tests cover truncation, alias preservation, irrelevant payloads, fallback order and merge precedence. The helper does not redact text, validate numeric cost types, attach currency/provider/model/token dimensions, preserve an evidence digest or bound the full issue-comment length; safe JSON byte constants are defined but not enforced inside this module.
units.designRationale: Keep live/list responses and issue comments useful without returning entire provider payloads.
units.companyOsProblem: Connector outputs need safe structured projection while raw evidence stays governed and immutable.
units.companyOsFit: Reference the projection-before-display idea only. Company OS requires a versioned Result envelope, typed usage/cost, sensitivity labels, evidence digest and separate localized presentation mapper.
units.responsibilityConflict: Free-form adapter summary posted as a durable work comment can be mistaken for verified result evidence and may contain sensitive content unless every caller redacts correctly.

units.function: Infers normalized run stop reason and timeout metadata from adapter type/config, outcome, error code and English error message.
units.dependencyDirection: Pure helper embeds Paperclip adapter names/config keys and is called from Heartbeat finalization.
units.keyDataModels: Outcome, stop reason, effective timeout, configured/source/fired flags.
units.lifecycle: Read timeoutMs/timeoutSec with adapter-specific defaults, infer reason, then merge metadata into result JSON.
units.testAssessment: Seven tests cover local defaults, configured timeout, budget/manual cancellation, graceful interruption, max-turn normalization, inconsistent success and merge. Critical gaps: local coding adapters default to unlimited timeout; budget/paused cancellation is inferred from English message substrings; invalid/negative config silently becomes zero; no Connector-declared reason/version is required.
units.designRationale: Normalize heterogeneous adapters enough for UI/diagnostics without changing every adapter result.
units.companyOsProblem: Connector-neutral execution needs authoritative, stable terminal reasons and bounded timeout policy.
units.companyOsFit: Do not reuse. Company OS Connector SDK must emit typed terminal reason/error code and negotiated timeout/cancellation semantics; deployment/risk policy supplies bounded defaults and invalid values fail closed.
units.responsibilityConflict: Misclassifying a manual cancellation as budget pause changes organizational meaning, and an unlimited default can leave delegated authority running indefinitely.

units.function: Many-to-many association service between issues and generic approvals with same-company validation.
units.dependencyDirection: Thin DB service couples Paperclip issue and approval schemas; routes decide who may add or remove links.
units.keyDataModels: Composite issueId/approvalId link plus duplicated companyId.
units.lifecycle: Validate both records share a company, insert idempotently, list either direction or delete the link at any approval status.
units.testAssessment: Tests cover tenant validation, idempotent link creation and deletion. No immutability/status rule prevents post-decision relinking, and no digest or revision records the association used when a human decided.
units.designRationale: Allow one approval to be surfaced from several related work items without embedding arrays in either row.
units.companyOsProblem: Responsibility projection needs immutable, versioned links from an approval receipt to exact work/action/evidence objects.
units.companyOsFit: Same-tenant foreign-key validation is worth retaining conceptually, but Company OS should create append-only responsibility edges inside the proposal transaction and supersede them only through a new contract revision.
units.responsibilityConflict: Post-resolution mutation can change what the audit trail appears to say was approved.

units.function: Best-effort helper that wakes an assigned non-backlog Agent with issue/task references after assignment-related mutations.
units.dependencyDirection: Issue routes inject the large Heartbeat service; helper knows its source/reason/context vocabulary.
units.keyDataModels: Issue ID/assignee/status, mutation/reason, task key and requester attribution.
units.lifecycle: Skip unassigned/backlog, enqueue assignment wake, swallow/log failure unless explicitly configured to rethrow.
units.testAssessment: No focused test belongs to this unit. Call sites mostly mock it, leaving exact idempotency, responsibility resolution, status races and failure policy unproven.
units.designRationale: Centralize repeated issue-assignment wake payload construction and avoid making ordinary mutations fail on transient scheduler errors.
units.companyOsProblem: Work assignment must reliably dispatch once and preserve initiator/responsible-human/action-contract context.
units.companyOsFit: Do not reuse the fire-and-forget helper. Company OS should persist a transactional dispatch outbox with idempotency/action digest and let a delivery worker call AgentExecutionPort.
units.responsibilityConflict: Wake payload contains attribution but no responsibility contract or exact permission/data grant; swallowed failure can leave assigned work silently undispatched.

units.function: Builds dependency-resolution wake idempotency keys and queries for existing wake requests in selected states.
units.dependencyDirection: Thin DB helper depends directly on the Heartbeat wakeup table; actual dependency transition and enqueue behavior lives in Issue routes/services.
units.keyDataModels: Dependent/blocker IDs, company-scoped idempotency key and wake status.
units.lifecycle: Derive deterministic key, query one existing non-skipped wake for one or several legacy/current keys.
units.testAssessment: No focused unit test exists; route integration covers three dependency/child-terminal scenarios. The schema has no general unique constraint for this idempotency-key family, so check-then-insert can race; 'claimed' is omitted from one related liveness idempotency set and status sets vary across helpers.
units.designRationale: Avoid duplicate Agent wakes when several blocker/parent transitions converge.
units.companyOsProblem: Event-driven work dependencies require atomic deduplication and replay-safe dispatch.
units.companyOsFit: Deterministic causal keys are useful, but Company OS must enforce uniqueness at the dispatch store and compare command digest, not rely on preflight reads with scattered status lists.
units.responsibilityConflict: Deduplicating by issue IDs does not prove the wake uses the same responsible human, work revision or execution authorization.

units.function: Persistence service for one active recovery action per company/source issue. It exposes active lookups, source-scoped upsert with attempt accumulation, and guarded terminal resolution, while preserving recovery owner, return owner, cause, fingerprint, evidence, wake/monitor policy and outcome.
units.dependencyDirection: The service imports shared recovery types but is implemented directly against the Paperclip Drizzle database and issue_recovery_actions table. An in-process promise queue serializes upserts per company/source issue; PostgreSQL partial unique indexes are the cross-process correctness backstop.
units.keyDataModels: IssueRecoveryAction with sourceIssueId, optional recoveryIssueId, kind, active/escalated/resolved/cancelled status, ownerType, ownerAgentId/ownerUserId, previous and return Agent owners, free-form cause/fingerprint/evidence/nextAction, wakePolicy, monitorPolicy, attempts, timeout, outcome and resolution note.
units.lifecycle: Read the current active or escalated action; update it and increment attempts when present; otherwise insert; retry up to three times on compare-and-update loss or the two named PostgreSQL uniqueness conflicts. Resolution updates every matching active row selected by company/source plus optional action/kind/cause/fingerprint filters.
units.testAssessment: A focused fake-DB race test proves that an action resolved after the initial read is not reactivated. The 2,110-line embedded-Postgres/API suite exercises source and tenant scoping, repeated upsert, typed fingerprint dedupe, no nested recovery, active projections, wake payloads, hand-back, stale folding, peer-Agent rejection, named-owner resolution, blockers, false positives, provider quota and recovery cause routing. Gaps remain for two-process races, crash/fault injection, retries exhausted, malformed JSON evidence/policies, human owner semantics, delete/retention, outbox atomicity and property-based state transitions.
units.designRationale: Model recovery as a durable first-class action attached to the original work instead of recursively creating recovery work, and make active uniqueness survive process concurrency through database constraints.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs first-class, source-scoped incidents/recovery cases with stable identity, bounded attempts, exact responsible human, executor, permission/data/approval contract digests, evidence references and a durable resolution receipt.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the partial-unique active case, compare-and-update anti-reactivation guard, typed cause/fingerprint, attempt history and explicit return-owner concept. Implement a Company OS RecoveryCase aggregate and store port with optimistic versioning/outbox; use opaque Principal IDs for human and Agent owners, append-only attempts and typed policies rather than Paperclip table rows and free-form JSON.
units.responsibilityConflict: The default owner is an Agent or an abstract board, ownerUserId is not part of the default selection rule, and previous/return ownership is Agent-only. A named Agent may resolve board-owned work. The record does not bind an accountable human, authority scope, data contract, approval digest or immutable evidence manifest; updating the same row also overwrites earlier evidence and policy.

units.function: Seventeen-file recovery subsystem that classifies stranded work and issue-graph liveness, retries or escalates assignment/continuation/review failures, watches silent active runs, creates source-scoped recovery actions, schedules provider-quota waits, repairs dependency wakes, and terminalizes orphaned runs/stale issue locks.
units.dependencyDirection: Pure policy helpers import shared types, but the 5,813-line service directly imports Drizzle schema, budgets, issues, execution policy, activity log, process supervisor, run-log storage, settings, redaction and Heartbeat enqueueWakeup. Recovery is therefore an orchestration monolith coupled to Paperclip issue/run/Agent storage and local process semantics rather than a portable domain boundary.
units.keyDataModels: HeartbeatRun, AgentWakeupRequest, Issue, IssueRelation, IssueRecoveryAction, WatchdogDecision, RunEvent, IssueComment metadata, execution policy/state, liveness finding, recovery origin/fingerprint, retry classification, model-profile hint, pause hold and successful-run disposition evidence.
units.lifecycle: Scan persisted work and runs; suppress on active paths/interactions/pause holds/operator cancellation; classify terminal failures; perform bounded retries or provider-quota monitors; upsert source-scoped recovery action; block/escalate with structured comment metadata; wake an Agent owner; separately scan issue-graph dead ends, silent runs and stale locks; retire obsolete recovery issues and clear terminal references. Several updates are transactional or guarded by unique indexes/advisory locks, while many cross-table issue/comment/activity/wake effects remain sequential and only partially idempotent.
units.testAssessment: Six colocated focused tests cover model-profile hint scrubbing, provider error text classification, one-shot review-path recovery with one DB uniqueness matcher, pause retry classification, structured stranded notices, and successful-run missing-disposition handoff including untrusted-text fencing. Major service paths are not covered inside this unit; external recovery/watchdog/stale-lock tests remain separate pending units. Gaps include multilingual/provider-structured failures, crash points across sequential side effects, distributed scheduler races, general wake-key uniqueness, accountable-human owner routing, Connector pause/cancel receipts, permission/data-contract digests and property-based graph recovery.
units.designRationale: Prevent assigned work from silently losing its execution or review path, keep automatic repair bounded, preserve human operator cancellation and pause holds, surface ambiguous success as a missing-disposition incident, and make failure recovery visible rather than leaving live-looking stale rows.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a canonical Recovery application capability for bounded retry, durable wait, responsibility-aware escalation, crash recovery, stale execution leases, graph dead ends, provider quota and explicit successful-run disposition. It also needs typed recovery causes and receipts across managed-cloud and self-hosted execution nodes.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the source-scoped recovery action, bounded retry, operator-cancel exemption, pause hold, successful-run disposition, untrusted-evidence fencing, stale-lease compare-and-set, recovery fingerprint/cooldown and explicit observability patterns. Re-express them behind Company OS ports with a durable command/outbox, typed Connector terminal events, exact work/responsibility/data/approval digests, human-first escalation policy and separate RecoveryPolicy, RecoveryProjection and ExecutionLease owners.
units.responsibilityConflict: Recovery owner selection is predominantly Agent reporting chains, creator Agents and hard-coded CTO/CEO roles; board is a fallback value rather than an accountable human principal with authority. Several recoveries reassign and wake Agents without binding the original responsible human or immutable permission/data contract. English error/output classification can change routing meaning, and best-effort/sequential wake/comment/audit writes can leave authority and execution state divergent.

units.function: Company-scoped recovery report that computes weekly recovery actions per Heartbeat run, threshold alerts, cause/error-code groups, takeover versus self-recovery and hand-back outcomes, and per-cause routing counters.
units.dependencyDirection: Pure handoff classification and rate-alert functions sit beside a Drizzle/PostgreSQL report service. The report queries Heartbeat runs, recovery actions and source Issues directly, using raw SQL for weekly/cause aggregation and TypeScript for low-volume handoff derivation.
units.keyDataModels: WeeklyRecoveryRate, RecoveryRateAlert, RecoveryCauseGroup, RecoveryHandoffSummary, RecoveryCauseRouting and RecoveryObservabilityReport derived from HeartbeatRun, IssueRecoveryAction evidence and final Issue assignment/status.
units.lifecycle: Clamp the requested window to 1-104 Monday-anchored UTC weeks; query run and action counts; fill missing weekly buckets; evaluate a configurable alert; group causes and latestRunErrorCode; join actions to final Issues; classify active, self-recovered, handed-back, owner-completed, board-owned or other; return ratios and routing totals.
units.testAssessment: Twelve tests cover threshold crossing, quiet/latest cases, six handoff classifications, embedded-Postgres rate aggregation, routing ratios and the allocation cap. The suite does not test tenant leakage adversarially, query plans/large volume, zero-denominator interpretation, mutable final assignment changing history, action-to-run cardinality, incomplete current week semantics, timezone boundaries, human ownership, alert delivery or metric version compatibility.
units.designRationale: Make recovery regressions measurable and expose whether managers are permanently taking over work rather than restoring the intended execution path.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs responsibility and autonomy safety metrics: intervention rate, retry/escalation/approval outcomes, time to accountable-human response, evidence completeness, authority/data-scope violations and whether work returned to the intended executor.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the normalized recovery-rate, bounded reporting window, pure classifier and explicit routing taxonomy. Build metrics from immutable domain events/receipts with versioned definitions and human/Agent principal dimensions; separate operational recovery health from organizational effectiveness and never infer historical responsibility solely from mutable current assignment.
units.responsibilityConflict: The metric's product goal is manager Agent takeover and its owner taxonomy is Agent versus board. Historical handoff is inferred from the Issue's current assignee, so later reassignment can rewrite the apparent outcome. Recovery actions divided by runs can also exceed one-to-one and should not be described as a failure probability without a stable event definition.

units.function: Best-effort annotation of an active Heartbeat run with one of two responsible-user authorization denial codes plus live-status publication.

units.testAssessment: Three mocked tests cover code filtering, scoped update fields and live-event payload. They do not verify real SQL conditions, races, cancellation/pause, durable audit, repeated denials, terminalization or propagation to Connector control.

units.responsibilityConflict: The run stays queued/running and only its errorCode changes; recording is fire-and-forget. This is observability, not enforcement of human responsibility.

units.function: Pure classifier that combines run status, issue state, persisted activity counts and English output heuristics into liveness/actionability/next-action labels.
units.dependencyDirection: Server helper imports only shared status types; the 19k-line Heartbeat service builds its inputs from many DB tables and persists its result.
units.keyDataModels: RunLivenessState, actionability, continuation attempt, evidence counters, next action and last useful action timestamp.
units.lifecycle: Normalize evidence, strip transcript noise, regex-classify blockers/approval/manager review/runnable language, then label success as completed/blocked/advanced/plan-only/follow-up/empty.
units.testAssessment: Fourteen focused tests cover planning-only, empty output, evidence, planning exemptions, blockers, durable-comment precedence, approval language, production review and background-process loss. They are English-fixture tests only; no multilingual, adversarial phrasing, false-positive corpus, structured Connector signal or confidence calibration exists. Counting any non-bookkeeping activity/tool event as progress does not prove successful useful work.
units.designRationale: Detect Agents that narrate future work without acting and bound automatic continuation without another model call.
units.companyOsProblem: Agent Boss needs honest liveness and bounded recovery across vendors, languages and deployment profiles.
units.companyOsFit: Use only as an optional low-confidence UX heuristic. Company OS canonical liveness must come from structured Connector progress/pause/evidence/result events, state transitions and deadlines; approval or risk routing can never depend on text regexes.
units.responsibilityConflict: Agent-controlled text can declare or hide approval/blocker language, while generic event counts can falsely imply progress. Neither is proof of permission, accountable-human approval or result evidence.

units.function: Special-case human decision that locks a stalled in-review issue, writes an optional attributed comment and moves it to done or todo.
units.dependencyDirection: Issue-specific service calls issue attention, issue mutation and activity services inside one DB transaction; authorization and wakeup remain in the route.
units.keyDataModels: Issue review-attention state, approve/request-changes action, human note/comment and status transition.
units.lifecycle: Lock issue row, re-check stalled state, persist raw human note as a comment, mutate status and record activity; route then syncs comment and best-effort enqueues resume.
units.testAssessment: Integration tests cover human/operator gates, hidden existence, stale/covered review conflict, row-lock concurrency, attributed injection-shaped note stored as data and reference-only wake payload. The broader route suite also proves an Agent can change reviewPolicy from human_only to anyone in the same verdict patch and then complete the issue, a serious policy self-relaxation gap. Post-commit wake insertion can fail after the decision becomes non-retryable.
units.designRationale: Offer a fast recovery path for reviews whose original interaction/approval path disappeared while preserving user notes as content, not instructions.
units.companyOsProblem: Review recovery must remain possible but cannot become a second weaker approval engine or permit policy self-modification.
units.companyOsFit: Use the row lock, state re-check and reference-only prompt-injection boundary as tests for the canonical Decision engine. Do not create a parallel special-case approval path; resume must use the same durable effect/outbox ledger.
units.responsibilityConflict: Generic non-viewer membership substitutes for designated reviewer authority, the route owns authorization outside the transaction, and policy can be relaxed by the acting Agent on another path.

units.function: Resolves whether an authenticated Agent run is a persisted task-watchdog execution and restricts its Issue mutations to the watched non-watchdog subtree or the reusable watchdog Issue.
units.dependencyDirection: The scope resolver directly reads Heartbeat runs, Issue watchdogs and parent-linked Issues through Drizzle. HTTP routes consume the returned tagged scope; the module has no dependency on those routes.
units.keyDataModels: Agent run actor, HeartbeatRun contextSnapshot.taskWatchdog, active IssueWatchdog, watched Issue, watchdog Issue and a maximum-100-level parent ancestry traversal.
